UI_AllInfo_note_translations: Skill and moodle descriptions are translation files. They cannot be switched off here; disable the mod to remove them.
UI_AllInfo_opt_Ammo: Ammo: rounds left and what it fits
UI_AllInfo_opt_Ammo_tip: No comparison arrows here: the thing in your hands is a gun, not another magazine, so there is no honest pair to compare.
UI_AllInfo_opt_AnimalGate: Animals: keep vanilla's Animal Care level requirements
UI_AllInfo_opt_AnimalGate_tip: Off by default, so you see everything from level 0. Turn it on and each row reappears at the Animal Care level vanilla itself uses for it: pregnancy at 3, weight at 5, attitude at 5.
UI_AllInfo_opt_AnimalInfo: Animals: butchering yield, milk, wool and old age
UI_AllInfo_opt_AnimalInfo_tip: Adds rows to the animal window you get by right-clicking an animal: meat yield, blood, feathers, old age and weight ceiling, which no screen shows, plus health, hunger, thirst, attitude, milk, wool and pregnancy as numbers instead of words.
UI_AllInfo_opt_Books: Books: reading time and skill levels covered
UI_AllInfo_opt_Books_tip: Reading time already accounts for Fast Reader, Slow Reader and reading glasses.
UI_AllInfo_opt_Clothing: Clothing: numbers on every bar, plus discomfort
UI_AllInfo_opt_Clothing_tip: Vanilla draws condition, insulation, wind, water, blood, dirt and wetness as bars with no figures. This writes the figures next to them and adds the discomfort value, which vanilla never shows at all. The run and combat speed modifiers get a signed figure too, which vanilla only ever draws as a bar with no sign.
UI_AllInfo_opt_Container: Bags: how much they slow you down
UI_AllInfo_opt_Container_tip: The run and combat speed a bag costs you, which the game applies and never shows. The run figure is the one you are paying right now: a bag's penalty grows by half again as it fills up, so the same pack goes from -3%% empty to -4.5%% full. It counts the same in your hands as on your back.
UI_AllInfo_opt_CookingWarmUp_tip: Off by default. Cooking time is the time at temperature; this adds the four minutes the food spends heating up before it starts to cook, so an oven timer set to the figure rings when the food is done.
UI_AllInfo_opt_CraftingTooltips: Crafting: full item tooltip on the recipe output
UI_AllInfo_opt_CraftingTooltips_tip: Hovering the result of a recipe shows the same block an item in your inventory would, comparison included, before you craft it.
UI_AllInfo_opt_CropInfo: Crops: health, growth and water as numbers
UI_AllInfo_opt_CropInfo_tip: Adds rows to the crop window you get by right-clicking a plant: health out of 100, current phase, hours to the next one, water level against what the plant needs, time since the last watering and pest levels.
UI_AllInfo_opt_FarmingGate: Crops: keep vanilla's Farming level requirements
UI_AllInfo_opt_FarmingGate_tip: Off by default, so you see everything from level 0. Turn it on and each row reappears at the Farming level vanilla itself uses for it: phase and health at 2, water at 3, pests at 3, next phase at 6.
UI_AllInfo_opt_Firearm: Firearms: range, jam chance and reload
UI_AllInfo_opt_Firearm_tip: Puts numbers on the condition and damage bars, and adds accuracy, effective range, jam odds and magazine size.
UI_AllInfo_opt_FishingGate: Fishing: keep vanilla's Fishing level requirements
UI_AllInfo_opt_FishingGate_tip: Back to vanilla's rules: Time needs Fishing 2, Temperature 4, Weather 6, Wind 8, and a species tells you nothing until you have caught it.
UI_AllInfo_opt_FishingGear: Fishing gear: rods, lines, hooks and baits
UI_AllInfo_opt_FishingGear_tip: Adds rows to the inventory tooltip: how fast a line wears out, how much each hook helps and which fish a bait attracts.
UI_AllInfo_opt_FishingInfo: Fishing panel: what each rating is worth
UI_AllInfo_opt_FishingInfo_tip: Right-click water and pick Fishing. Puts the real multiplier next to Time, Temperature, Weather and Wind, adds hook, spot, bite chance and waiting time, and explains each one on hover.
UI_AllInfo_opt_FoodInfo: Food: time left before it spoils
UI_AllInfo_opt_FoodInfo_tip: Adds hours to stale and hours to rotten, at the current rate. Accounts for the fridge, the freezer and the sandbox spoilage speed.
UI_AllInfo_opt_FuelPumpInfo: Gas pumps: fuel left and power source
UI_AllInfo_opt_FuelPumpInfo_tip: Adds an Info entry to the right-click menu of any gas pump, with the fuel still in the tank and whether the mains or a generator is keeping it running. The game knows that number and only prints it as a debug option.
UI_AllInfo_opt_GeneratorHighlight: Generators: outline the powered area on the floor
UI_AllInfo_opt_GeneratorHighlight_tip: Draws the edge of the range while the generator window is open, green when running and red when off. Only the floor you are standing on is computed.
UI_AllInfo_opt_GeneratorInfo: Generators: fuel time, wear and danger
UI_AllInfo_opt_GeneratorInfo_tip: Adds noise radius, hours of fuel left, average time until 20%% condition and until it breaks, and the hourly odds of a backfire or a fire.
UI_AllInfo_opt_GeneratorRealTime: Generators: also show times in real-world minutes
UI_AllInfo_opt_GeneratorRealTime_tip: Off by default. Converts the in-game hours using the current day length, so you know how long you actually have to wait.
UI_AllInfo_opt_HealthGate: Wounds: keep vanilla's Doctor level requirements
UI_AllInfo_opt_HealthGate_tip: Off by default, so you see everything from level 0. Turn it on and each row reappears at the Doctor level vanilla itself uses for it: scratches and lacerations at 3, deep wounds and splints at 5, fractures and stitches at 7, wound infection at 9.
UI_AllInfo_opt_HealthInfo: Wounds: how long each one still needs
UI_AllInfo_opt_HealthInfo_tip: Adds an Info entry under the treatments you get by clicking a body part in the health panel. Hover it and the box beside it gives the time left on every wound, what bandaging or a poultice would save, how long the bandage lasts and whether the part is mending or getting worse. The game knows all of it and only prints it in debug mode.
UI_AllInfo_opt_HideFishingCombat: Fishing gear: hide the combat stats
UI_AllInfo_opt_HideFishingCombat_tip: Rods, nets and fishing spears are weapons in the game's own scripts, so they get crit chance, swing type, attack speed and knockback. This drops that block on fishing gear. The condition and damage bars are drawn by the game in one call and cannot be removed by any mod.
UI_AllInfo_opt_MedicineDetail: Medicine: the full list of effects
UI_AllInfo_opt_MedicineDetail_tip: Off by default. Adds everything else each pill does: what cancels it, what intoxication costs it, and the sleeping tablet overdose table.
UI_AllInfo_opt_MedicineInfo_tip: Painkillers, beta blockers, antidepressants, sleeping tablets and antibiotics get how long they last, how long they take to start and what they do per minute. Every figure is recomputed from the sandbox day length.
UI_AllInfo_opt_MeleeWeapon: Melee: exact damage, speed and durability
UI_AllInfo_opt_MeleeWeapon_tip: Puts numbers on the condition and damage bars, and adds crit chance, swing type, attack speed, knockback and the odds of losing a condition point per hit.
UI_AllInfo_opt_MoodleTooltip: Moodles: description box that fits its text
UI_AllInfo_opt_MoodleTooltip_tip: The game's own moodle box is two lines tall and cuts off anything longer, which is most of AllTheInfo's descriptions. This draws the moodle column itself so the box grows with the text. Turn it off to go back to the vanilla widget.
UI_AllInfo_opt_Nutrition: Food: calories, carbs, protein and fat
UI_AllInfo_opt_Nutrition_tip: Off by default. Showing macros on every food undoes the Nutritionist trait, which is what normally reveals them.
UI_AllInfo_opt_Power: Batteries and radios: charge left, how long it lasts and how far a torch lights
UI_AllInfo_opt_Power_tip: Vanilla draws the charge of a drainable as a bar with no number on it, and never says how long a torch lasts or how far it lights. A torch spends its UseDelta once every ten game minutes, and only while it is in a hand or attached to you: left in a bag it switches itself off. Light range and strength are the figures that actually light the ground.
UI_AllInfo_opt_RecordedMedia: Tapes and CDs: which skill they teach and how much XP
UI_AllInfo_opt_ShowDeltas: Show the difference against what you have equipped
UI_AllInfo_opt_ShowDeltas_tip: Adds a coloured +/- next to weapon and clothing values. Weapons compare against what is in your hands, clothing against the piece worn in the same slot.
UI_AllInfo_opt_SkillRecipes: Skills: which recipes each level requires
UI_AllInfo_opt_SkillRecipes_tip: Hover a level in the skills panel to see the recipes and builds that ask for it. Read from the game's own recipe list, so modded recipes appear too and nothing goes stale with a patch.
UI_AllInfo_opt_Sleep: Beds: how well you recover on them
UI_AllInfo_opt_StructureBuildMenu: Build menu: health of what you are about to build
UI_AllInfo_opt_StructureBuildMenu_tip: Also shows what that health would be with the relevant skill at 10, so you can tell whether it is worth waiting.
UI_AllInfo_opt_StructureInspect: Walls and doors: health under the cursor
UI_AllInfo_opt_StructureInspect_tip: Shows current and maximum health as a number at the foot of whatever you point at, no clicking needed.
UI_AllInfo_opt_TraitInfoCreation: Character creation: what each trait and job really does
UI_AllInfo_opt_TraitInfoCreation_tip: Adds starting skill levels with their true XP multiplier, free traits granted, recipes taught and foraging bonuses to the tooltips in the creation screen.
UI_AllInfo_opt_TraitInfoScreen: In game: the same block on the info tab
UI_AllInfo_opt_TraitInfoScreen_tip: Hover a trait icon or the job icon in the character info tab to read the same block after the world has started.
UI_AllInfo_opt_TraitManualEffects_tip: Effects hardcoded in the game's Java that cannot be read at runtime, so they are written by hand and checked against each build.
UI_AllInfo_opt_TrapGate: Traps: keep vanilla's Trapping level requirements
UI_AllInfo_opt_TrapGate_tip: Off by default, so you see everything from level 0. Turn it on and the trap tooltip only appears from Trapping 3, which is the level vanilla itself uses elsewhere.
UI_AllInfo_opt_TrapInfo: Traps: catch odds, bait and hours
UI_AllInfo_opt_TrapInfo_tip: Adds an Info entry to a placed trap: the odds of it catching anything in an hour, which animals it can take and the share of the catch each one gets, the bait and its freshness, the zone, the hourly odds of losing bait or trap, and the warning that a trap catches nothing while you stand next to it. Bait foods get a row naming what they attract.
UI_AllInfo_opt_XpMultiplierFix: Show XP boosts as a multiplier, not a percentage
UI_AllInfo_opt_XpMultiplierFix_tip: Vanilla says "+75%%" for a level 1 boost. The real figure is x4, because a skill with no boost runs at a quarter rate. Fixed on all three screens that show it.
UI_AllInfo_perk_Alarm: %1%% chance of setting off the car alarm

UI_AllInfo_perk_AnimalStress: %1 points off the chance a stressed animal breaks off milking or shearing

UI_AllInfo_perk_Dismantle: %1%% chance of recovering material when dismantling
UI_AllInfo_perk_EngineHeavy: you can salvage and repair a heavy-duty engine
UI_AllInfo_perk_EngineSport: you can salvage and repair a sport engine
UI_AllInfo_perk_EngineStandard: you can salvage and repair a standard engine

UI_AllInfo_perk_Hotwire: %1 points to the chance of hotwiring a car
UI_AllInfo_perk_MedInfection: you spot a wound infection straight away
UI_AllInfo_perk_MedPain: you can read pain, and spot the burns that need washing

UI_AllInfo_perk_RecipesOnly: no effect of its own, this level only unlocks the recipes below
UI_AllInfo_perk_RipCloth: %1 rags when you rip up clothing, capped by the parts it covers
UI_AllInfo_perk_ShearTime: %1%% time per litre shearing an animal
UI_AllInfo_perk_ThreadPick: %1 to the most thread you can pick out of a garment

UI_BEP_TQW_Note1Body:
WANTED - DEAD OR ALIVE

%1

Wanted for looting the Rosewood depot and for killing two of our own.

REWARD: 4 crates of ammunition and a tank of gasoline.
Deliver proof at the mile 12 outpost.

- The Accountant
UI_BEP_TQW_Note2Body:
Mom:

If you're reading this, someone found me before you did.
We're not the monsters they talk about on the radio. At first we just wanted food.
After what happened at the farm... I don't know what we are anymore.

Don't come looking for me.

%1
UI_BEP_TQW_Note3Body:
STANDING ORDER - READ AND BURN

1. No one enters the perimeter without the password.
2. The wounded stay behind. No exceptions.
3. If one of us falls, call it in on the radio and regroup. Do NOT give chase.
4. Whoever abandons their post answers to me.

Signed: %1
UI_BEP_TQW_Note4Body:
WHAT THEY OWE ME:

- Vic: 200 rounds of .308. Dead. Collected.
- Marta: the shotgun. Took off up north.
- The new guy: nothing yet. Good aim, though.
- %1 (me): a shot to the knee I took covering all of them.

Nobody ever pays up.

UI_BFP_blockPath_tt: Cancels the vanilla zombie AI pathing a bandit to a player it cannot see. Paths towards a noise are left alone.
UI_BFP_debug_tt: Writes what the fixes are doing to the console. Only useful when reporting a problem.
UI_BFP_guardTolerance_tt: How far from the exact tile still counts as holding the post. 15 means one and a half tiles.
UI_BFP_hearDist_tt: How close you have to be before a bandit notices you without seeing you. Also caps the Recon and Tracker bonuses.
UI_BFP_lootClothing_tt: Puts the clothing a bandit was wearing onto its body. Turn this off if another mod already does it.
UI_BFP_mapBandits_tt: Marks every bandit close enough to be loaded on the world map and the minimap: red for hostiles, blue for your companions. It cannot show the whole county - only what your game is already loading around you, so a group still warns you before you can see where it came from. Turn it off if you would rather not know.
UI_BFP_mapCompanions_tt: Draws friendly NPCs on the map as well, in blue. Applies to both of the other map options.
UI_BFP_mapSymbols: Also place them as map symbols (for second-screen map mods)
UI_BFP_mapSymbols_tt: Second-screen map mods such as PZ Map redraw the map themselves and cannot see the overlay above, so this registers the bandits as real map symbols instead, which they do read. Warning: map symbols are your saved annotations. They are removed again every second and when you switch this off, but if the game is killed outright a few stamps can be left on your map for you to delete by hand. Off by default for that reason.
UI_BFP_markerClear: Hide the warning once they are dead
UI_BFP_markerClearDist_tt: How close you must be to the marked spot before an empty area counts as 'all dead' rather than 'not loaded yet'.
UI_BFP_markerClear_tt: Removes the warning as soon as no bandit of that side is left alive nearby.
UI_BFP_markerLive_tt: Points the arrow at where the closest living bandit is right now, instead of the tile the group spawned on.
UI_BFP_markerMerge_tt: Several groups arriving in a row stack arrows on top of each other. Keeps only the newest one per side.
UI_BFP_memory_tt: After losing sight of you, bandits search where they last saw you for this long. Set to 0 to make them forget instantly.
UI_BFP_minimapBandits: Also show them on the minimap
UI_BFP_minimapBandits_tt: The minimap is on screen the whole time, so bandit dots there mean you always roughly know where they are. Turn this off to keep them on the world map only, which you have to open on purpose. Has no effect unless the option above is on.
UI_BFP_protectMode_tt: What friendly NPCs are allowed to break. Hostile bandits are never restricted.
UI_BFP_softGuard_tt: Lets a companion hold a post it is standing next to, instead of looping between the post and you.
UI_BFP_stealth: Bandits notice you only by sight or sound
UI_BFP_stealth_tt: Limits the AI's player sensor to line of sight, hearing at close range, or being attacked - the same rules zombies play by.

UI_BFP_watchdogSeconds_tt: How long an NPC has to fail to move before the watchdog resets it.

UI_BN_Bs_breaker_demo_intro_f: {name} took buildings apart for a living. Doors and barricades are barely an inconvenience.

UI_BN_Bs_breaker_locksmith_intro_m: {name} worked as a locksmith, and few things stay shut for long once he sets his mind to it.

UI_BN_Quest_antibiotics_desc: I want to understand how this thing really spreads. Bring me {count} courses of antibiotics for the research -- and I'll teach you a thing or two about patching people up.
UI_BN_Quest_antibiotics_success: "Fascinating, and horrifying. Here -- let me show you what I've learned."
UI_BN_Quest_cigs_desc: I'd trade an arm for a smoke. Bring me {count} packs and I'm yours.
UI_BN_Quest_doll_desc: If you ever come across a little doll out there... I lost my daughter's when we ran. I'd just like to hold one again.
UI_BN_Quest_doll_success: "...yeah. That's the one. Thank you. I won't forget this."
UI_BN_Quest_drink_desc: Find me a bottle of something strong. Just one. Helps me sleep without the dreams.
UI_BN_Quest_drink_success: "...I'll make it last. Probably won't. Thanks."
UI_BN_Quest_escrap_desc: Get me {count} bits of electronic scrap and I'll show you how to keep the lights on after everyone else is in the dark.
UI_BN_Quest_escrap_success: "See? Power's just patience and not electrocuting yourself. Your turn."
UI_BN_Quest_fuel_desc: There's a place I keep dreaming about -- the dark down past the warehouses. I'm not ready to go back. Bring me a can of fuel and I'll tell you what I saw there. Take this torch; you'll want it.
UI_BN_Quest_fuel_success: "...the doors were chained from the inside. Whatever did that wasn't trying to keep things OUT."
UI_BN_Quest_games_desc: Stupid thing to miss, but I'd kill to play something again. Find me {count} old video games? Even if there's no power to run them yet.
UI_BN_Quest_games_success: "Ha! Look at that. Maybe one day we hook up a generator and a TV. Deal?"
UI_BN_Quest_generic_hunt: Thin the herd -- take down {count} zombies.
UI_BN_Quest_hunt_desc: I keep hearing them at night. Thin the herd for me -- {count} of them -- and I'll sleep a little easier.
UI_BN_Quest_hunt_success: "Quieter now. Thank you. Get some rest."
UI_BN_Quest_mags_desc: Anything to read would help. Bring me {count} magazines or comics and I'll be a happy idiot.
UI_BN_Quest_mags_success: "You're a lifesaver. Don't spoil the endings."
UI_BN_Quest_saucepan_desc: Find me a saucepan and I'll turn our sad cans into something that tastes like a memory. I'll teach you, too.
UI_BN_Quest_saucepan_success: "A hot meal changes everything out here. Take this pot -- and what I showed you."
UI_BN_Quest_scalpel_desc: For the next stage I need a proper scalpel. What I'm studying... it's not pretty. But it might matter. Help me and I'll pass on what I know.
UI_BN_Quest_scalpel_success: "...the things in their blood shouldn't move like that. Anyway. You earned this knowledge."
UI_BN_Quest_screwdrivers_desc: Bring me {count} screwdrivers and I'll teach you how to keep a car breathing. We don't get far on foot.
UI_BN_Quest_screwdrivers_success: "Engines don't lie to you. People do. Here, this'll help you."
UI_BN_Quest_soda_desc: Bit silly, but... could you find me {count} cans of soda? I just miss the taste. Normal things, you know?
UI_BN_Quest_soda_success: "...ice cold would've been perfect. Thank you. Really."
UI_BN_Quest_soup_desc: Food's been thin. Could you bring me {count} cans of soup?
UI_BN_Rec_food_prompt: "I'll travel with you, but I'm running on empty. Got any food to spare?"
UI_BN_Rec_food_refusal: "Sorry... bring me something to eat first."
UI_BN_Rec_none_prompt: "Honestly? I've got nowhere else to be. I'll come with you."
UI_BN_Rec_water_prompt: "My throat's like sandpaper. Got anything to drink? Then we'll talk."
UI_BN_Rec_water_refusal: "Not until I get something to drink."
UI_BN_Rec_weapon_prompt: "I'm not stepping out there empty-handed. Spare me a melee weapon and I'm yours."
UI_BN_Rec_weapon_refusal: "Find me a weapon first, then we'll talk."

UI_BN_TopicRX_rumor_farm_Cook: "Forget growing it -- it's about not wasting it. A root cellar, some salt, and I can stretch one deer through a whole winter. Find the food; I'll make it last."
UI_BN_TopicRX_rumor_farm_Tracker: "Follow the deer. Where they graze, the land's still good. There's an orchard gone wild south of the farms -- apples for the taking if the bears don't beat you to it."
UI_BN_TopicRX_rumor_farm_Trapper: "You don't need a farm -- you need a snare line and patience. Set traps along the game trails by the creek and you'll never go hungry. I'll show you the spots."
UI_BN_TopicRX_rumor_mil_Assasin: "I wore the uniform. The Knox facility wasn't a containment site -- it was a research lab. They knew weeks before they warned anyone. We were ordered to hold a line we were never told the truth about."
UI_BN_TopicRX_rumor_mil_Recon: "I scouted that perimeter before the fences went up. Heavy vehicles, comms towers, men who didn't answer questions. Whatever this is, it started behind those gates."
UI_BN_TopicRX_rumor_safe_Recon: "That forest bunker's no myth -- I've stood on its hatch. Concealed entry off an old logging trail northeast of the lake. Whether anyone's still home is another question."
UI_BN_TopicRX_rumor_safe_Tracker: "Safest place is wherever the herds aren't, and that changes daily. But the deep woods past the ridge? They don't wander up there. I'd build there if I were settling down."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_cook: "Find me an onion and a little heat and I'll make you forget it's the end of the world. For one plate, anyway."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_elec: "Give me a generator, some fuel, and ten minutes where nothing's trying to eat me. Hot showers again -- imagine that."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_mech_1: "You treat the clutch like it owes you money. But you keep us moving, so I'll allow it."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_mech_2: "Every time you grind the gears, a little piece of me dies. Otherwise? Not bad."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_med_1: "That scratch says otherwise. Sit. Let me look before it turns -- they ALL turn now."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_med_2: "'Fine' is what people say right before they spike a fever. Humor me and roll up your sleeve."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_recon: "Spent years where the only map was the sky and the moss on the trees. Towns turn me around. The wild never does."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_sold: "No. I don't. Some doors you don't open out here. Just know I'm good in a fight, and leave it at that."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_thief: "Ha. Relax. Old habits, sure -- but I don't steal from the people who watch my back. ...Probably."
UI_BN_TopicR_ban_trap: "Rabbit, mostly. Fat one yesterday. Out here a snare line beats a gun -- quiet, and it works while you sleep."
UI_BN_TopicR_boss: "I'm not your dog. Watch your tone with me."
UI_BN_TopicR_deep: "With you? Maybe. For the first time, I think maybe."
UI_BN_TopicR_doubt: "That's rich, coming from you. Fine. Whatever you say, boss."
UI_BN_TopicR_flirt: "...I feel the same. Have for a while now."
UI_BN_TopicR_jeal_cold: "...wow. Noted. I'll keep my feelings to myself from now on, then. Lesson learned."
UI_BN_TopicR_jeal_confront_1: "...you didn't deny it. I don't know whether to be grateful you're honest or furious you did it. Both, probably."
UI_BN_TopicR_jeal_confront_2: "I won't ask you to choose -- the world's too small and cruel for that. Just don't make me feel like a fool."
UI_BN_TopicR_jeal_reassure: "...words are cheap, but I want to believe you. So don't make a liar of me. Please."
UI_BN_TopicR_joke: "Heh. That was awful. I needed it."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_cook: "Heat, timing, and never wasting a scrap. Pay attention."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_elec: "Rule one: assume every wire is live and wants you dead. Now, slowly..."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_fight: "Alright. Breathe out when you swing, don't flail, and never back into a corner. Again."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_mech: "Pop the hood. A car's just a thousand small problems that trust each other. Here."
UI_BN_TopicR_learn_med: "Sit. First rule: stop the bleeding, then worry about the pain. Watch my hands."
UI_BN_TopicR_nag_1: "...wow. I'm doing my best out here, same as you."
UI_BN_TopicR_nag_2: "Charming. Want to trade packs and find out how heavy it is?"
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_close: "...about time. Don't let go, alright? Not tonight."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_fear: "Every single day. That's why I watch your back like I do. Don't you dare die on me."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_future_1: "A house with a door that locks for the right reasons. A garden. You, complaining about my cooking. That's the whole dream."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_future_2: "Quiet. Just quiet, and you next to me. I stopped wanting more than that a long time ago."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_love: "...I love you too. Saying it feels dangerous, like it can be taken away. But it's true."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_notice_1: "...I've noticed. I don't mind. Bit of warmth in all this -- I'll take it."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_notice_2: "Yeah? And here I thought I was being subtle about watching you back."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_open: "...then don't. I'm tired of pretending too. Whatever this is -- I want it."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_partner: "You and me. To the end of it. I'm not going anywhere -- you're stuck with me now."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_start: "...I was hoping you'd say that. Yes. Whatever this is -- let's find out together."
UI_BN_TopicR_rom_stop: "...oh. Right. No, I get it. Friends, then -- I'd rather have that than lose you."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_dark_1: "A school. I won't describe it. Just... don't go to the one off the highway. Promise me."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_dark_2: "They move different at night. In packs. Almost like they remember how to hunt. I don't sleep much."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_farm_1: "The farms out past the treeline. Animals gone feral, fields gone wild, but a smart forager eats like a king out there."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_farm_2: "McCoy land had logging cabins with stocked larders. Far from the roads. Far from help, too."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_loot_1: "Warehouses down by the river. Everyone hit the pharmacies first -- nobody thinks about the loading docks."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_loot_2: "The gun store in town was stripped day one. But the houses behind it? People left in a hurry. Doors still unlocked."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_loux_1: "The big city? They walled it and it didn't matter. Millions behind that concrete. If you go in, you don't come out -- but the mall never got picked clean..."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_loux_2: "Louisville's a graveyard the size of a county. Army dropped the bridges to slow them. Whatever's behind the wall is still in there, pacing."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_march: "March Ridge, maybe. Small, fenced. There were army trailers parked at the south end before the end -- supplies, if the looters left any."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_mil_1: "The Knox facility up north was ground zero. Whole region got sealed off -- nobody who went to look came back."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_mil_2: "There was a checkpoint on the bridge to West Point. By the end they were turning survivors away at gunpoint."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_muld_1: "Muldraugh's a one-road town -- gas station, warehouses, a sawmill. The horde rolls down Main Street like a tide. Loot the edges, never the middle."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_muld_2: "There's a storage lot in Muldraugh nobody bothered with. Padlocks, mostly. If you've got a sledge and nerve, might be worth it."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_river: "Riverside's quieter -- rich little river town. Big houses, full pantries, folks who locked up tight and never made it back. Watch the gated streets."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_safe_1: "People whispered about a prepper's bunker out in the forest. Could be a myth -- could be the last dry bed in the county."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_safe_2: "The Rosewood fire station had a solid setup before it got overrun. Might still be worth a look, if you're brave."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_signal_1: "A looping emergency message, mostly. But one night I swear I heard a real voice -- a woman, giving coordinates. Then static. I've wondered ever since."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_signal_2: "The official channels went dead weeks ago. Anything you hear now is either a recording... or someone who shouldn't still be out there talking."
UI_BN_TopicR_rumor_west: "West Point's got everything and ten thousand of them to guard it. The pharmacy and the gun store are gold -- if you can stand the noise you'll make getting out."

UI_BathTowelsOverhaul_WipeMySelfMode_too:
In this mode, even if the body is not wet, if there is dirt or blood on it, "Dry Self" will be available. *When "Dry Self", wetness, dirt, and bloodstains will be wiped off as much as possible from the body. (Normally, only up to 20%% of the dirt on the body can be wiped off at once.) *If the "Dry Self Context Tooltip" is displayed, the player's dirt and blood status will also be displayed.
*In vanilla, dirt and bloodstains on the body do not have much of a negative effect, but other mods may cause dirt and blood to cause health problems or attract zombies, so this is useful in such cases. However, you will need to wash your towel more frequently.

UI_Bounty_bobby_1_desc: Building secondary barricades. Cash paid for boxes of nails and screws.
UI_Bounty_bobby_2_desc: To explore locked warehouses I need a solid crowbar and a working flashlight.
UI_Bounty_caleb_1_desc: Hunting season requires sharp knives to process animal meat and hides.
UI_Bounty_chloe_1_desc: We have hungry mouths to feed today. I need canned meals and a sturdy can opener.
UI_Bounty_chloe_2_desc: I need a sharp kitchen knife, matches for the stove, and breakfast cereals.
UI_Bounty_dave_1_desc: We are reinforcing vehicle defenses. I need a welding mask and a working blowtorch.
UI_Bounty_dave_2_desc: I need to repair the water pumping system before our clean water reserve runs out.
UI_Bounty_dave_3_desc: Paying well to anyone who brings a full propane tank for the workshop.
UI_Bounty_derek_1_desc: Securing our safe zone entrance. Looking for a police nightstick and a double holster.
UI_Bounty_derek_2_desc: Patrol sidearms need fresh ammo boxes. Handgun rounds are high priority.
UI_Bounty_elena_1_desc: Our shortwave radio receivers drain batteries quickly. Flashlights needed too.
UI_Bounty_evelyn_1_desc: Several survivors have open wounds. We urgently need sterile bandages and disinfectant.
UI_Bounty_evelyn_2_desc: A patient has high fever and bacterial infection. I require antibiotics and alcohol wipes.
UI_Bounty_evelyn_3_desc: We have run out of needles to close deep laceration wounds.
UI_Bounty_gwen_1_desc: We are tilling new soil for winter crops. I need a shovel and fresh water bottles.

The cups were from a donation drive last year, branded with a church logo and a slogan about salvation. The irony was noted but not discussed. Discussion was for people who had calories to spare on talking.

For {{openerName}}, these pages are hot soup in paper form: {{skillNameA}} first, because the body needs to be capable before the mind can be useful. {{recipeName}} second, because the mind needs to know how to feed the body even when the church donations stop and the cups run out and the only thing left is what you can make yourself from what's left in the pantries of people who don't need pantries anymore. {{traitName}} third, because surviving the holidays still counts as a miracle even when the angels are all dead and the herald angels aren't singing anything except the emergency broadcast on a loop.

If you can carry {{traitName}} without spilling it, without letting it leak out and make you vulnerable, without letting it become a burden that slows you down when you need to move - carry it. If you can't, leave it here with the cups and the names and the thin soup. Some gifts are too heavy for some people. That's not failure. That's just physics. That's just the reality of what you can hold versus what the world keeps piling on. Take what you can. Leave what you must. Keep moving. That's the gift that matters: motion, continuation, the refusal to become part of the scenery, the scenery that is increasingly full of things that don't move except to chase things that do.
UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideToy:
The toy store was untouched because nobody wanted to admit children still existed. We took batteries, blankets, and one stuffed rabbit that smelled like smoke. {{noun}} {{verb}} in the back room and every music box started at once.

{{openerName}} can have the notes on {{entryNameA}} and {{entryNameB}}. Leave the toys unless you need something soft enough to remember mercy.
UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideTre:
The tree farm smelled so normal it hurt. Pine, mud, gasoline, and somebody's old thermos coffee. We cut branches for camouflage and pretended the wreaths on the office door were not covering bullet holes.

{{survivorName}} left {{supplyNoun}} there for strangers. I left {{entryNameA}} and {{entryNameB}} for the same reason. If {{openerName}} hears bells in the rows, do not follow them.
UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideWar: This was wrapped for {{openerName}} with one last bit of {{adjective}} mercy. Keep {{supplyNoun}} close and make it through the week. {{exclamation}}.
UI_BurdJournals_LoreTemplate_YuletideWor:
The workshop is not at the North Pole this year. It is any garage with a locked door, any kitchen with a sharp knife, any clinic with one clean bandage left. Good people make gifts out of whatever keeps someone breathing.

So here: {{entryNameA}}, {{entryNameB}}, and a little note saying {{exclamation}}. {{openerName}} can decide which part is festive.

UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_AnyAdvice:
When you enter the arena, remember you are part of the installation. Perform with vigor.

The more spectacular your... decommissioning of the other exhibits... the more valuable the echoes you'll yield for my collection.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_CanWeBargain:
Haggle? With me?

My good fellow, I have acquired treasures from ruins history itself has forgotten.

My price is the final word.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_Default:
I am the Curator.

You are standing inside my masterpiece.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_TheUndead:
Marvelous, aren't they?

The zombies provide such a wonderful sense of physicality.

The ghosts, on the other hand, offer a more... ethereal aesthetic.

A balanced collection needs both.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_TryHonestyWager:
Ah. You're the one he sent. Of course you are. Try Honesty never comes himself when pride might be spared by distance.

Yes, I kept the Brass Bout Bell. He lost it fairly, however loudly he may remember otherwise. A fountain was used, the terms were broken, and the bout ceased to be a bout at all.

He believes a cheering crowd can correct a ruined condition. He is wrong. Frequently, and with style.

Still, I am told you performed well. Better than most of the meat he throws into that pit. That gives me hope.

So take the bell. Not as settlement of his grievance, but as an investment in yours.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_TryHonestyWagerCla:
The Brass Bout Bell is yours now.

Take it back to Try Honesty. I am certain he will mistake retrieval for vindication.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_WhatDoYouSell:
I provide the tools for the exhibits to... refine themselves.

I accept the resonant echoes left behind by the... decommissioned performers... and in return, I lend out superior artifacts to those who show promise.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_WhatIsThisPlace:
You are in the Carrion Ascension.

The centerpiece of my exhibition on mortal transience and posthumous endeavor.

The fights below are a... dynamic sculpture. A study in conflict.
UI_CHCurator_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
I am the Curator.

This crypt, this arena, the very echoes that cling to the air... all of it is part of my permanent collection.

You are standing inside my masterpiece.
UI_CHCynthiaElias_Bubble_Entry01:
Cynthia: Someone's here, Elias. Do you feel it? They feel... real.
Elias: I know... The whole place felt it, sister.
Cynthia: Do you think they've come for us?
Elias: If they have, the Warden will find them first.
UI_CHCynthiaElias_Bubble_Entry02:
Cynthia: They're inside. Elias... they really went in. Why would it let them in?
Elias: It shouldn't have... Maybe it wants something from them.
Cynthia: That's what worries me.
UI_CHCynthiaElias_Bubble_Entry03:
Cynthia: They're really going down there?
Elias: Hm. Seems so.
Cynthia: The Warden must think highly of them... if he's letting them near Father's arena.
Elias: I don't think that's why he let them through.
Cynthia: Then we'll see what he wants with them.

UI_CHLyra_Bubble_Intro:
Careful with the cards you clutch so tightly. Some of their threads run deeper than this crypt, down past the bedrock, into a place the church stopped naming.

She listens there. She likes curious hands.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_CallasFamily:
In the records, the Callas look immaculate: the family appointed to stand between the church and the place below, after the first archivist - the one they bound down there - the one that had to be contained.

The wards beneath don't listen to prayers. They listen to blood. Callas blood opens doors other people can only die in front of.

So the church called it duty. Privilege. Legacy.

She reads it differently. To her, the Callas line has always been a promise: that where the margins of her own bloodline bled into theirs, a Callas girl would be born more key than child - ink and Callas blood braided into a vessel made to fit the one below.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_Default:
Careful with the cards you clutch so tightly. Some of their threads run deeper than this crypt, down past the bedrock, into a place the church stopped naming.

She listens there. She likes curious hands.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_UndyingOnes:
You call them undying.

I see bodies whose stories were cut wrong and stitched back by a will that refuses endings.

Some of what's wrong here is older than that. Those people died the way people are meant to.

Flesh to soil, breath to silence. It's their souls that never made it out - thin, stubborn echoes pinned here, because this estate and the place below drink from the same poisoned vein.

The others are different. They went down into the place below and left too much of themselves within her reach.

What crawled back up wears their meat, but there isn't a story inside anymore... just hunger, hanging off a borrowed thread.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_UnspoiledGraceAccepte:
Then we ask water to remember what it was before it learned to bargain.

Find the vial Marlowe kept. Untouched grace can rinse noise from a vision without teaching it to bite back.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_UnspoiledGraceTurnedI:
There. The thread finds its pattern again.

The static recedes, and the image of the Sanctum begins to gather back into shape. You did well.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_WhatAreTheseCards:
On the surface?

Just pictures, numbers, promises. Underneath, they're pages torn from lives that already happened - memories that slipped the binding.

Each card is an echo of a story you never got to live. When you hand me a set, I press that story into one shape and give it a body again.

You call it an item.
I call it... closure.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_WhereFindCards:
Anywhere the place below brushes against the surface.

They cling to things that kept moving after their story should have stopped, and to those who walked too far into the wrong corridors and didn't come back whole.

If a road feels like it's straying toward the depths, watch what falls there.

The cards are drawn to that kind of ruin.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
Who am I...?

That depends which one of you is asking.

Up here they write it as Lyra, Weaver of Threads. Sounds tidy, doesn't it?

As if any of this was done on purpose.

I listen to the loose strands that got caught in your cards - the bits of you that almost were, or were once already.

I give them something solid to become, and you walk away thinking it was just a trade.

As for who I was before...

She remembers better than I do.

The one below.

I try not to use her name; it has a habit of answering back.
UI_CHLyra_Dialogue_WhoIsShe:
She was the one who filed other people's truths into neat little rows. An archivist, breathing dust and ink, lingering in the forbidden margins no one was meant to read.

Then the words stopped lying still for her. They slipped off the page, wound themselves around her thoughts... and a few important stitches came loose.

The church called it heresy. The place below called it an opening.

Now she's more pull than person - a will moving along the deeper threads, looking for a loose one like yours to tug.

I don't use her name. Names are doorhandles, and she's very good at turning them.
UI_CHLyra_DivinationUnavailableSay: Lyra's transmutation is not available right now.
UI_CHMarlowe_DialogueOption_WhatDeals: What kind of deals does it offer?
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_AreYouControllingI:
Controlling it? Good heavens, no.

I simply understand its manners better than most.
My dear friend, everyone uses something. Tools, faith, fear, other people. I am merely more polite about it.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_ChooseYourFateAcce:
Excellent. The fountain is waiting, and it adores decisive customers.

Take one bargain. Any one. Return when the water has marked the transaction, and I will release the vial.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_ChooseYourFateTurn:
There we are. Paid in consequence, sealed by the fountain, witnessed by a man of impeccable bookkeeping.

Take the vial to Lyra. And do try to remember who kept it safe all these years.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_Default:
Ah, a customer. Or a pilgrim. Hard to tell these days.

Either way, welcome.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_RepeatGreeting1: Back again? Wonderful. I was beginning to worry you had developed caution.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_RepeatGreeting2: Come to bargain, or merely to stare at the consequences?
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_RepeatGreeting3: Careful near the water. It has a talent for overhearing desire.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_RepeatGreeting4: Ah. My favorite kind of visitor. Alive, curious, and not yet sufficiently warned.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhatDeals:
Useful ones. Dangerous ones. The sort people swear they would never accept, until they need them badly enough.

Strength for frailty. Fortune for hunger. Clarity for something you may miss only after it is gone.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhatDeals_Response: Most bargains do, when described honestly.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhatIsFountain:
Once? A holy little thing, I am told. Graceful, generous, terribly inefficient.

Now? It has matured.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhatIsFountain_Res: A blessing for a consequence. That is how the fountain speaks now.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhoAreYou: <accent>Marlowe Veyne</accent>. Collector of rare opportunities, negotiator of regrettable wishes, and, on better days, a perfectly respectable gentleman.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhoAreYou_Response: Charlatan is such an ugly word. I prefer... <accent>specialist in selective truths</accent>.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhyOutHere:
Because this is where people come when prayer has failed, coin has failed, and good sense has failed most of all.

And because the fountain and I have an understanding.
UI_CHMarlowe_Dialogue_WhyOutHere_Respons: I bring it the desperate. It reminds them that nothing worth having arrives cleanly.
UI_CHMarlowe_PlayerResponse_Charlatan: That sounds like a lot of words for charlatan.
UI_CHMelora_Bubble_Intro:
Cynthia, if Mr. Klaus sees you out late again... oh.

You're someone else. Forgive me.

The water keeps returning the wrong reflections.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_Default:
Cynthia, if Mr. Klaus sees you out late again... oh.

You're someone else. Forgive me.

The water keeps returning the wrong reflections.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_DoYouNeedHelp:
No... no, I'm fine.

I have everything I need.

But... if you do see Julian, tell him I'll be waiting.

Just a little longer.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_NeverMind:
Of course.

The water's better company, anyway.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
The name is Melora.

I work the kitchens.

Sometimes I help with the little ones when the mistress isn't looking.
UI_CHMelora_Dialogue_WhyOutHere:
Oh, I like it here.

It's quiet.

The water listens better than people do.
UI_CHMothersCrypt_FoundSomethingInCoffin: I found something in the coffin!
UI_CHQuestLog_a_bell_in_the_ruins_DescRi:
You woke with the sound of a bell in your head.
In the dream, you saw a ruined church beneath a dead sky. Its doors stood open.
Below the floorboards, candlelight flickered.
You do not know why it matters.
But a church may still mean shelter, supplies, or answers.
UI_CHQuestLog_choose_your_fate_DescRich: Marlowe has the Vial of Unspoiled Grace, and no intention of releasing it for something as cheap as gratitude. He calls the fountain honest: one blessing, one consequence, every miracle properly accounted for. Accept one bargain from the fountain, then return to Marlowe and collect the vial.
UI_CHQuestLog_lyra_the_unspoiled_grace_D: Lyra's visions of the Sanctum are drowning in corrupted divine noise. The fountain's current waters would only turn memory into a bargain. Marlowe holds a Vial of Unspoiled Grace, drawn before the curse. Find him by the courtyard fountain behind Callas Manor and recover it.
UI_CHQuestLog_serevine_relic_altar_DescR:
Serevine returns the Sanctified Bell to you,
not as a trophy, but with a purpose.
She believes the altar in the chamber beside her was made to receive relics such as this, allowing their sacred influence to endure while bound within it.
Place the Sanctified Bell into the relic altar, then return to Serevine.
UI_CHQuestLog_serevine_relic_altar_Objec: Place the <accent>Sanctified Bell</accent> into the <accent>relic altar</accent>
UI_CHQuestLog_serevine_the_bell_below_De:
Serevine believes the bell seen in your dream may be the Sanctified Bell, a sacred Valerian relic once sealed somewhere beneath Cedar Hill Church. If she is right, then your dream was no mere imagining.
Descend deeper into the church cellars, uncover the hidden reliquary, recover the Sanctified Bell, and return it to Serevine.
UI_CHQuestLog_serevine_the_callas_record:
Serevine has exhausted the church's surviving records of the Sanctuary. They confirm that it once existed, but reveal nothing of its location, its purpose, or the reason it was hidden. The Callas family may have preserved what the church concealed.
Travel to Callas Manor and uncover any record they left behind concerning the Sanctuary.
UI_CHQuestLog_silas_ashen_wards_DescRich:
Silas has heard the dead of House Callas stirring within their family cemetery. The wards etched upon their stone coffins are failing, leaving their rest exposed to whatever stirs below.
Take the warding kit, repair the broken wards, and return to Silas once the graves have fallen silent.
UI_CHQuestLog_silas_the_invitation_DescR:
Silas believes you have earned an introduction. With the Regal Hatch Key in hand, the way to the Carrion Ascension now lies open.
Beneath the opposite crypt waits an arena few living souls are invited to see.
Descend through the hatch and present your invitation to Try Honesty.
UI_CHQuestLog_silas_unquiet_crypt_DescRi: Silas has entrusted you with a grim task. The Mother's Crypt is poisoned by a sorrow that has festered into rage, unsettling the peace of the graveyard. He has given you the key, and charged you to enter the crypt, find the source of the turmoil, and put it to rest by any means necessary.
UI_CHQuestLog_silas_warden_call_DescRich:
You heard a voice near the Callas Family Cemetery...

"Ah, a living soul... a rare and welcome sight these days. If you have a moment for an old warden, come, let us speak."

Find the source of the voice among the graves, and learn what stirs there.
UI_CHQuestLog_the_servants_way_DescRich:
Explore the Estate. While the right path leads to the old graveyard, the left fork remains largely unexplored.
It winds past the estate's overgrown greenhouse and down toward the waterline. Perhaps the servants who once walked this route knew secrets their masters had long since forgotten.
UI_CHQuestLog_tryhonesty_crowd_wants_mor:
Try Honesty is not done with you yet.
The crowd has seen you survive. Now they want to know whether you can win without leaning on the fountain like a wounded noble at a garden party.
Complete one full arena match without using the fountain, then return to Try Honesty.
UI_CHQuestLog_tryhonesty_first_match_Des:
Try Honesty has accepted your invitation,
though not without making a spectacle of it.
The Carrion Ascension does not hand out glory freely. Step into the arena, survive one full match, and return to Try Honesty with your dignity mostly intact.
UI_CHQuestLog_tryhonesty_gentlemans_wage:
Try Honesty has decided your survival may yet be useful. An old wager with the Curator ended poorly after a match was soured by technicalities, excuses, and one very inconvenient fountain.
Ask the Curator about the wager, recover the Brass Bout Bell, and return it to Try Honesty.
UI_CHQuestSay_silas_unquiet_crypt_comple: The spirits... they're finally at peace.
UI_CHQuestSay_silas_warden_call_complete: The old warden... what tales he must hold.
UI_CHQuestSay_tryhonesty_crowd_wants_mor: The fountain broke the challenge. I will have to try again.
UI_CHQuestSay_tryhonesty_first_match_com: I made it through the arena.
UI_CHQuestSay_tryhonesty_gentlemans_wage: The bell is back where it belongs.

UI_CHSerevine_Bubble_Church01:
Stop right there. Not a step closer!
...Oh. A person. And alive?
Wonderful. Alarming, but wonderful.
Come in, then. A fellow explorer, I hope.
UI_CHSerevine_Bubble_Church02:
Sorry. You startled me half to death, which is very rude in a place already full of death.
I'm Serevine, Valerian scholar, temporary cellar resident, and currently very grateful you are not trying to eat me.
UI_CHSerevine_Bubble_Church03: Oh, it worked! There is something different about you now. A steadiness, perhaps... as though the Bell has finally found its proper bearer. Leave it upon the altar, and I believe its blessing will remain with you.
UI_CHSerevine_DialogueOption_CallasMap: Is that a map of Callas Manor?
UI_CHSerevine_DialogueOption_DeadWalk: Any idea why the dead walk?
UI_CHSerevine_DialogueOption_DreamChurch: I saw this church in a dream
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_CallasMap:
It is. Remarkable, isn't it?

Every wing, every garden path, even the servants' passages have been recorded in extraordinary detail.

I had expected a parish sketch. This is something far more deliberate.

Though it has one rather curious omission.

The records place Valerian's first sanctuary somewhere beneath the estate.

Yet this map makes no mention of it at all.

For a place of such importance to be absent from a map this precise... I find it very difficult to believe that was an oversight.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_DeadWalk:
Nothing I could honestly call an answer.

But I have found records of visits to a Valerian sanctuary on the Callas estate. Supposedly, the first sanctuary ever raised in His name.

If that is true, it is extraordinary. Thousands of years of history, doctrine, relics... perhaps even accounts from the founding of the faith itself.

I confess, I was rather thrilled when I first understood what I was reading.

Then I reached the later entries. The visits become fewer. People return from the sanctuary described as distant... vacant... diminished.

One account says a man came back breathing, walking, and speaking... yet his wife insisted that whatever returned from beneath the estate was no longer her husband.

I would very much like to dismiss it as frightened superstition. Given what is wandering outside, that has become rather difficult.

If there is an answer beneath the Callas estate, I think we ought to find it.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_DreamChurch:
This church? Before you had ever set foot inside it?
How extraordinary.

Forgive me. I imagine it was rather less extraordinary to experience.

Dreams of sacred sites do appear in old Valerian studies, though never in any account I considered reliable.

There is one detail those accounts repeat with peculiar consistency.

Tell me, did you hear a bell?
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_HeardItRinging:
You did?
Then I may owe several long-dead scholars a sincere apology.

I had always assumed they were describing a symbol, not an actual phenomenon.

Judging by the state of the steeples, I sincerely doubt the tower bell has rung for a very long time.

Yet the accounts describe a bell heard in sleep, calling the living toward sacred ground.

I thought it devotional allegory.

Now you are standing here, in the very church those accounts describe. Which makes this considerably more important than I had hoped.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_RelicAltarAccepte:
Take it. Not as a trophy, but with a purpose.

The altar in the nearby chamber was made to receive relics such as this. If the bell is placed there, its influence may endure without being carried in your hands.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_RelicAltarTurnedI:
Then it worked. There is something steadier in the air now, as though the Bell has finally found its proper bearer.

Leave it upon the altar, and I believe its blessing will remain with you.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_TheBellBelowAccep:
Then we should treat your dream as evidence, however inconvenient that may be.

The accounts speak of a bell beneath holy ground. If the relic is here, it will not have been left in any ordinary chamber.

Descend below the church. Find what the Valerians sealed away, and bring the bell to me before you bind it to anything.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_TheBellBelowTurne:
You found it. Valerian's Bell... and not merely a story after all.

There is a sanctified mark beneath the tarnish. Give me a moment with it. If the old rite still answers, I can return it to you as something more than salvage.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_TheCallasRecordAc:
The church records have taken us as far as they can.

If the Callas family concealed what the Church could not admit, their manor may still hold the missing account. Recover any record they left behind concerning the Sanctuary.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_TheCallasRecordTu:
This is exactly what I feared, and exactly what I needed.

The Callas record gives shape to the omission. Whatever lies beneath that estate was not forgotten. It was deliberately hidden.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_WhatIsThisPlace:
I had hoped it was only a hidden archive. The scrolls, the sealed records, the fireplace kept for long nights of study... those I can understand.

Though judging by the dust, no one has studied here in centuries.

The cages in the corridor are rather harder to explain. Rust, brittle leather, dust thick enough to bury a confession.

Whatever happened here, it happened long before the dead began walking.

There are restraints here. Instruments meant for questioning, if one wishes to be charitable.

Whatever was recorded in this room, I do not think it was always offered willingly.

That is the part I find most troubling. The restraints bear Valerian seals. The records beside them carry the same insignia.

Whoever used this place was not hiding from the Church. They were acting in its name.
UI_CHSerevine_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
I study Valerian relics, sacred sites, and the history people usually find more comfortable leaving buried.

I came to Cedar Hill after hearing the rather extraordinary accounts surrounding Callas Manor.

My superiors thought the matter warranted investigation.

Truthfully, I would have come whether they asked or not.

UI_CHSilasAshenWards_ExamineFirst: I should examine the seal first.
UI_CHSilasAshenWards_NeedSealKit: I need Silas' seal kit for this.

UI_CHSilas_Bubble_Intro: Greetings, traveler. I am <accent>Silas</accent>, the warden of this place. It is not often I receive visitors who still draw breath.
UI_CHSilas_Bubble_WardenCall: Ah, a living soul... a rare and welcome sight these days. If you have a moment for an old warden, come, let us speak.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_AshenWardsAccepted:
Take the kit. Its tools are modest, but they remember the shape of the old wards.

Examine the grave seals throughout the cemetery. If one answers wrong, correct it before the unrest spreads.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_AshenWardsTurnedIn:
Yes... I can feel it. The stones are quieter now.

You have given the dead a kindness, and the living a little more time.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_CanIHelp:
Perhaps. The wards around this cemetery have begun to fray in ways they should not.

If you are willing, I would ask you to inspect the grave seals, correct what has been miswritten, and return before the unrest deepens.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_Default: Greetings, traveler. I am <accent>Silas</accent>, the warden of this place. It is not often I receive visitors who still draw breath.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_InvitationAccepted:
Then the way is open. Take this invitation.

The place across the grounds will not welcome the living easily, but it should recognize the warden's seal.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_UnquietCryptAccepted:
I see you have taken an interest in the plight of this place. Thank you.

The Mother's Crypt holds a sorrow that has festered into rage.

It disturbs the peace of this entire ground.

Take this key. Enter, and pacify the source of the turmoil.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_UnquietCryptTurnedIn:
The crypt is still at last.

Whatever pain was bound below has loosened its grip. Rest may return to this ground.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
My name is Silas.

I am the keeper of this graveyard, a warden of memories and a tender of final rest.

I have watched over these stones for longer than I care to recall, ensuring the peace of those who reside here.
UI_CHSilas_Dialogue_WhyOutHere:
This is my purpose.

The living have their bustling cities, and the departed... have this.

Someone must ensure their slumber is not disturbed by the... restless energies that cling to Callas Manor.

It is a quiet duty, but a necessary one.

UI_CHTryHonesty_Bubble_Intro: How delightful. Silas has sent me another mortal who thinks they're meant for more. Give me the invitation. We'll see what survives.
UI_CHTryHonesty_Dialogue_ArenaRank: Your arena rank is shown below.
UI_CHTryHonesty_Dialogue_DoYouEnjoyThis:
Enjoy? That's the word mortals use when someone finally does what they were made for.

I don't enjoy it. I am it.
UI_CHTryHonesty_Dialogue_GentlemansWager:
You've got potential. A rare inconvenience. Most who enter my arena die too quickly to be of use to me.

The Curator and I once placed a gentleman's wager. A relic against the outcome of a bout. Then the match soured, a fountain was touched, and that shrivelled little priest of order decided the rules had been violated.

I say a fighter still breathing is a fighter still in the contest. He says otherwise. Naturally, he wrote the conclusion down and called it truth.

So he kept my stake. The Brass Bout Bell. Without it, the pit is mere spectacle. With it, the bout is sanctioned.

Go to him. Tell him I want the bell returned.
UI_CHTryHonesty_Dialogue_WhoAreYou:
Name's Try Honesty.

I build the trials that prove what you are and bury what you pretend to be.

UI_CVO_Options_ConeOutlineAlpha_Tooltip: Outline opacity (0 — barely visible, 1 — full brightness). Same idea as View Cone Opacity in game options.
UI_CVO_Options_ConeOutlineColor_Tooltip: Color of the outline for zombies and animals in the vision cone when aiming (RMB). Melee hit-list green outline is unchanged.
UI_CVO_Options_LegacyOutlineMode_Tooltip: Off by default. The mod now asks the game which zombies and animals it has already decided to draw, instead of guessing from square visibility and the mod's own vision-cone math. Turn this on to go back to the old guesswork if the new default ever looks wrong to you.
UI_CVO_Options_OutlineAlwaysOn_Tooltip: Off by default. When on, outlines are shown all the time, whether you are aiming (RMB) or not, on foot or in a vehicle. Overrides the vehicle-only option below, which still works fine on its own if you leave this off.
UI_CVO_Options_OutlineAnimals_Tooltip: When on, animals in the vision cone are outlined along with zombies. When off, only zombies are outlined. On by default.
UI_CVO_Options_ScaleOutlineByFog_Tooltip: Off by default. The game doesn't track fog per tile, only one thickness for the whole world at a time, so this approximates it: outlines fade toward the edge of your current clear-visibility radius (the same one the game itself uses), scaled by how thick the fog is right now. Has no effect at all outside of fog. Combines with 'Scale outline by light level' when both are on, and the cone outline intensity slider is the ceiling for the result. Works in both Legacy and the new default outline mode. Rarely, on certain scene geometry (thin posts/beams), an outline scaled by this or by light level can render behind that object instead of through it -- a limitation of the game's own renderer.
UI_CVO_Options_ScaleOutlineByLight_Toolt: Off by default. When on, the outline fades as the light on the target drops (darker = fainter, full dark = no outline). It reads the same light the game uses to draw the zombie itself, so your flashlight, lamps and fire all count, not just the ambient sky. The cone outline intensity slider is the ceiling: the outline holds that opacity in good light and only fades below it. Works in both Legacy and the new default outline mode. Rarely, on certain scene geometry (thin posts/beams), an outline scaled by this or by fog can render behind that object instead of through it -- a limitation of the game's own renderer.
UI_CVO_Options_VehicleOutlineAlwaysOn_To: When on, in a vehicle outlines are shown without holding RMB (aim/look). When off, same as vanilla: hold RMB to see outlines.

UI_DeadStash_ArchiveInfectedRoster: Acolytes, archive agents, quarantine rangers, desert chemists, patrol deputies, prototype mechanics and other former keepers may still carry a lead.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_AncientArena: An old arena tablet depicts mirrored strongholds and five champions; a modern surveyor proved that part of the legend reached Kentucky.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_AshTemple: A soot-stained survey places an impossible sanctuary over an ordinary Kentucky road. Its congregation hid the surviving ritual pieces before vanishing.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_AureliaRestorat: The Aurelia is a fully drivable original prototype. Its normal mechanical systems survive beneath a six-stage archival rebuild.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_BlackReliquary: Three keepers wrote the same warning: opening the black box after sunset calls ashbound guardians until dawn.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_BlueHorizonLab: A clandestine chemistry crew used a cobalt signature to mark precision equipment and a supply route through the desert.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_BrambleReserve: Bramble preserved living bloodlines as carefully as seeds. Completing the trail can return three named animals to the world.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_BreakerHouse: The breaker card records one manual switching sequence, a failed automatic trip and the diagnostic meter left inside the unmanned substation.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_BrokenDispatch: The county dispatch ledger preserves one unfinished transfer made after every official ambulance route had already closed.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_ChronorunnerGar: A sealed garage held a hand-built timing prototype, repaired electronics and a vehicle engineered to outrun consequences rather than time.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_Clocktower: A corrected blueprint describes a mechanism that measured distance instead of time. The clock stopped, but its brass heart remained.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_ColdGrid: A county priority ledger lists the buildings meant to survive a total outage, then crosses out every feeder except one maintenance circuit.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_DeadAirTrace: A damaged emergency-band transcript repeats a civil-defense call sign at fixed intervals, enough to reconstruct the first relay trace.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_DustlineTournam: A vanished exhibition match left only referee notes, weapon checks and the identities of competitors who never reached the final round.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_FirstTrail: A guided local trail designed to teach dossier reading, map marking, recovery and journal cataloguing.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_FrozenCrown: Coordinates hidden in a pulp-fantasy chronicle lead to a collection preserved where the air remained unnaturally cold.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_InfernalArcade: The thirteenth wave of a scorched arcade cabinet was never supposed to be finished. Its last player left a route behind.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_IonEdgeLab: An access card and incident log document an experimental ion tool, a failed containment drill and a laboratory abruptly erased from the books.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_IronAtlas: A grand strategy map is layered with production orders, alternate offensives and one last transfer to a forgotten depot.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_IsolatedFeeder: A hand-corrected feeder map leads to a buried line-crew cache and proves the surviving circuit was deliberately cut away from the county grid.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_KnoxBlackstart: The final order cannot restore the county grid. It isolates one safe circuit and leaves a yellow emergency generator connected for whoever arrived next.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_LastBroadcast: The blackout route leads to a mobile relay van abandoned after its crew sent one final emergency transmission.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_LastHighway: An oil-stained roadbook follows a courier through fuel stops and ambushes to a final shipment that never reached settlement.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_LastPatrol: A frontier patrol left practical weapons and weathered uniform pieces along the route of its final, unsuccessful rescue.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_LastReliefConvo: The last relief convoy never reached its public destination. A corrected waybill leads instead to the depot where its route ended.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_LunarArchive: Undeveloped film shows impossible survey frames over Kentucky and the final field cache of an archive team that disappeared.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_MercyWard: St. Peregrin's overflow ward buried its remaining supplies and sent one tagged responder ahead with the convoy papers.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_MidnightMuseum: An unofficial museum manifest records exhibits moved after midnight by a guard who knew the collection was never meant to be public.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_MothlightQuaran: Quarantine rangers documented a spreading fungal threat, then sealed their filters, samples and field pendant inside the cordon.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_NeonGhostVault: A damaged datashard reconstructs a courier route through a failed signal experiment and identifies the interceptor left behind.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_RedSunCheckpoin: Abandoned military orders connect a deserted roadblock, a missing armored ledger and a ranger vehicle awaiting recovery.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_RelayCalibratio: A field calibration sheet marks a buried alignment point where the relay crew adjusted its aerial before the blackout.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_ReserveCircuit: A sealed fuel docket places the blackstart reserve beneath an abandoned service yard and names the operator who carried the final synchronization order.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_ResonanceLab: An unscheduled resonance test, a missing crowbar and a sealed emergency manifest are all that survived the laboratory's final shift.
UI_DeadStash_ArchiveLore_Starfall: Redacted reports follow a silent object recovered after a flash over Kentucky and a containment team that abandoned its evacuation route.

UI_EHR_Codex_LockedDesc: Read the matching disease flyer or reach First Aid level 8 to unlock symptoms, causes, prevention, and treatment notes.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Cause: Receiving blood that is incompatible with your body.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Duration: 2-4 days without treatment; can become fatal quickly.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Prevention: Use compatible blood and test compatibility whenever possible.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Symptoms: Lower back pain, severe weakness, nausea, high fever, hemolysis, endurance loss, and dangerous health decline.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Treatment: IV fluids and furosemide are the main treatments. Antipyretics, anti-nausea tablets, and anti-inflammatory pills reduce symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Cau: Fungal spores from decomposing corpses in damp, wet, or cold conditions.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Pre: Wear face protection near damp corpse-filled areas and avoid breathing contaminated air.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Sym: Respiratory irritation, fever, coughing, wheezing, endurance loss, and weakness.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Tre: Bronchodilator inhaler and antipyretics for symptoms; antifungal tablets or IV amphotericin to cure.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Cause: A spreading bacterial skin infection after a poorly closed wound. Rough suturing has a high risk of starting cellulitis.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Prevention: Clean wounds before suturing, use sterile supplies, and avoid rough stitching when possible.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Symptoms: Hot red skin, swelling, local pain, fever, fatigue, weakness, and reduced endurance. Untreated stage 4 can progress into sepsis.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Treatment: Antibiotic ointment can treat mild cases. Prescription antibiotics, broad-spectrum antibiotics, plant-based antibiotics, IV antibiotics, or IV vancomycin treat more serious cases. Anti-inflammatory and antipyretic tablets reduce symptoms only.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Cause: Cold, wet, or prolonged exposure while exhausted.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Prevention: Stay warm, dry, rested, and protected from bad weather.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Symptoms: Coughing, sneezing, mild fever, fatigue, and reduced stamina.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Treatment: Rest, fluids, cough medicine, antipyretics for fever; Cold & Flu tablets or antiviral capsules can cure it over time.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Cause: A hard head impact from a height fall or serious vehicle crash.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Prevention: Avoid high falls and severe crashes. Treat head impacts as dangerous even if you can still walk.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Symptoms: Headache, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea, and disorientation that gradually improves over time.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Treatment: No direct cure. Rest and time are the main treatment; symptom medicine can make recovery easier.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Cause: Prolonged exposure to decomposing corpses, especially in enclosed spaces.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Prevention: Ventilate corpse-filled spaces and wear effective face protection.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Symptoms: Eye irritation, nausea, dizziness, weakness, coughing, and possible collapse at high exposure.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Treatment: Fresh air immediately. Anti-nausea tablets help symptoms; respiratory support kit or corticosteroids can treat severe cases.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Cause: Extreme stress held at its breaking point for many hours.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Prevention: Reduce stress before it reaches a prolonged maximum state.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Symptoms: Hallucinated sounds, irrational speech, visual distortion, and unsafe impulsive behavior.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Treatment: Antipsychotics. Requires an 8-dose course over 4 days.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Cause: Tainted water or severe gastrointestinal contamination.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Prevention: Drink clean or boiled water and avoid unsafe water sources.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Symptoms: Severe diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, fever, weakness, and possible blood loss.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Treatment: Electrolytes and anti-diarrheal medicine for symptoms; IV ciprofloxacin for severe bacterial infection.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Cause: Rotten food, burned food, or stale food.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Prevention: Eat fresh food and avoid food that has spoiled, burned badly, or gone stale.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, endurance drain, increased hunger and thirst.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Treatment: Anti-nausea tablets, electrolyte powder, and activated charcoal. Activated charcoal can cure it over time.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Cause: Eating with bloody or dirty hands.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Prevention: Wash hands before eating. Soap and clean water are best.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Symptoms: Severe nausea, vomiting, dehydration, stomach pain, and fatigue.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Treatment: Anti-diarrheal medicine, electrolyte powder, antiviral capsules, or IV ciprofloxacin for severe bacterial cases.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Cause: Heat exposure, dehydration, heavy clothing, or exertion in hot weather.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Prevention: Hydrate, rest in shade, wear lighter clothing, and avoid overexertion in heat.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Symptoms: Dizziness, nausea, weakness, thirst, fatigue, and overheating.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Treatment: Cool down, rest, drink water, and use electrolyte powder.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Cause: Extreme heat exposure or severe dehydration.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Duration: Critical until body temperature is controlled.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Incubation: Can develop from untreated heat exhaustion.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Prevention: Avoid extreme heat, hydrate aggressively, and treat heat exhaustion early.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Symptoms: Extreme body temperature, delirium, confusion, vomiting, collapse/blackouts, dehydration, and life-threatening health loss.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Treatment: Immediate cooling. Instant ice packs can cure heat stroke with a 4-dose cooling course; fluids and electrolytes help dehydration.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Caus: Prolonged exposure to contaminated dirt or grass. The first bite leaves a scratch-like wound.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Prev: Avoid lingering on bare dirt or grass when possible, cover exposed skin, and keep wounds clean.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Symp: Severe itching, repeated scratch wounds, bite-site pain, fever, and dangerous health decline in late stages.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Trea: Topical permethrin is the main treatment. Antiparasitic pills can also cure it, but the course is longer.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Cause: Low body temperature from cold, wet clothing, wind, or exposure.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Prevention: Wear insulation, stay dry, and get indoors during severe cold.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Symptoms: Shivering, weakness, confusion, fatigue, and dangerous temperature drop.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Treatment: Warm up, change into dry clothes, rest, and use external heat sources.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Cause: Prolonged extreme fatigue, caffeine crash, combat stimulant crash, or nitric oxide booster crash.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Incubation: Triggered after 12 hours at very high fatigue, or rarely after stimulant crashes.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Prevention: Sleep before exhaustion becomes prolonged and avoid stacking strong stimulants.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Symptoms: Poor rest, inability to sleep naturally in later stages, stress, fatigue, and headache.
UI_EHR_Codex_insomnia_Treatment: Sleeping pills allow sleep while active. Dual orexin receptor medication cures over 96 hours; antidepressants cure over 168 hours.
UI_EHR_Codex_knox_infection_Symptoms: Fever, nausea, weakness, pale skin, and terminal systemic infection.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Cause: Repeated use of regular or homemade painkillers, especially five or more doses within 24 hours or doses taken too close together.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Durati: Persistent. Stage 3 does not recover naturally.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Incuba: Develops after sustained or excessive painkiller use.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Preven: Avoid frequent redosing and keep daily painkiller use below the high-risk range.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Sympto: Craving, persistent stress and depression, and increased thirst. An active painkiller or buprenorphine dose temporarily suppresses withdrawal symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Treatm: Buprenorphine cures the condition over 120 hours: 10 doses, one every 12 hours. Each active dose suppresses withdrawal symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Cause: Severe or untreated respiratory illness, cold exposure, or weakened health.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Prevention: Treat respiratory illness early and avoid prolonged cold exposure.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Symptoms: Fever, coughing, chest pain, endurance loss, and potentially lethal respiratory failure.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Treatment: Prescription or broad spectrum antibiotics cure over time; IV Ciprofloxacin is the fast clinical cure. Bronchodilator helps breathing, cough medicine suppresses coughing, antipyretics reduce fever.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Cause: Untreated severe infection entering the bloodstream.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Prevention: Treat wound infections and cellulitis before they spread.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Symptoms: High fever, extreme weakness, confusion, rapid decline, and life-threatening systemic illness.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Treatment: IV antibiotics and aggressive medical support. This is an emergency condition.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Cause: Deep contaminated puncture wounds, rusty metal injuries, or severe dirty wounds.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Prevention: Clean deep wounds quickly and use tetanus prophylaxis when possible.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Symptoms: Jaw stiffness, muscle spasms, pain, fever, and dangerous neuromuscular failure.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Treatment: Muscle relaxants for symptoms; tetanus antitoxin or tetanus immunoglobulin with a syringe to cure.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Cause: Poisonous berries, poisonous mushrooms, or other toxic food.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Prevention: Avoid unidentified wild food unless you can verify it is safe.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Symptoms: Violent nausea, vomiting, dizziness, blurred vision, weakness, and dangerous systemic poisoning.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Treatment: Activated charcoal is the main treatment. Anti-nausea tablets and electrolytes help symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Cause: Raw or undercooked wild game and unsafe raw meat.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Prevention: Cook meat thoroughly, especially wild game.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Symptoms: Intense muscle pain, fever, weakness, and dangerous health loss in severe stages.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Treatment: Muscle relaxants and anti-inflammatory medicine for symptoms; antiparasitic pills or albendazole injection to cure.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Cause: Long-term respiratory exposure in contaminated corpse-heavy environments.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Prevention: Avoid prolonged corpse exposure and wear respiratory protection.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Symptoms: Persistent cough, fever, fatigue, weight loss, night sweats, and coughing blood in severe cases.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Treatment: TB antibiotics or rifampicin combo pack. Cough suppressants and antipyretics only reduce symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Cause: Dirty wounds, poor bandaging, or untreated injury contamination.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Prevention: Clean wounds, use sterile bandages, and change dirty bandages quickly.
