UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_44_Content:
Uncle Bob, the phone lines are still down, so it's just letters from me for the time being. Just wanted to let you know that I'm okay, despite everything that's been going down these past few days. I normally wouldn't have this much time to write, but our wing's on lockdown today. Can't separate the truth from the con talk these days, but what I do know is some sicko was caught eating his cellmate. We all saw the guy, covered in blood and grayer than the cold, hard concrete beneath our toes, getting wheeled out by the COs strapped to those chairs that they put Hannibal Lecter in. Yeah, straight out of the Silence of the Lambs movie, mask and all. I didn't know they actually had stuff like that! If he ever leaves the hole, which I sure as hell hope he doesn't, he'll be taking the nickname "Hannibal the Cannibal" to his grave. At least I have my trial date coming up this Friday; maybe the appeal will finally go through and you and I will get to hang out and go fishing again like the good old days. They keep delaying it, though, probably because of this new bug everyone's so afraid of now. I think it's another one of those bird flu things they sometimes talk about on TV; it's bad enough that they've
even got the army enforcing a quarantine around all of Knox County. Some cons in here are swearing on their own mothers that they knew so-and-so who caught this mystery bug, and that now they're in and out the infirmary running a really nasty fever. I wish they were lying, but more and more guys in here have been getting sick lately. Even a few COs are clocking out early saying they've got the "Knox bug". And you won't believe the kind of rumors this one nutjob is spreading around here about it. The guy's saying old Hannibal had the bug before anybody else, and that it's what caused him to lose his marbles and do what he did to his poor celly, like rabies or something. He rants on and on all night about how everyone who catches the bug is a ticking time bomb, and it's only a matter of time before we're all just like Hannibal the Cannibal. I told him he needed to stop taking everything he heard on KnoxTalk radio as the gospel of truth, and to zip it before someone less kind than myself landed him in the very same infirmary bed that all the sick folks are coughing, barfing, and vomiting all over. That sure as hell shut him up.

It's been four or five hours now, and the lockdown still hasn't been lifted. Apparently it's just our cell block anymore, but a total lockdown. Whatever's happening, I just hope the COs at least have the decency to serve us our lunches. Rumors are spreading wild now, and not just from the nutty guy. It seems everyone's got their own idea of why we're still on lockdown, and half of them are hiding under their pillows thinking that Hannibal broke loose and is coming back for seconds. You remember my cellmate, Hugh, the guy who does janitorial work around the jail? I've known Hugh going on for half a year, and he's not one to spout fairytales. He says he was mopping up when a CO, white like she'd seen the boogeyman, ran over and snatched the broomstick right out of his hands before hauling on back the way she came and jabbing it in between the handles of the canteen doors just before a whole lot of hands started banging on them from the other side. Hugh said that was about an hour before the lockdown started; he thinks somebody started a riot in there, and that's what's causing all this. Causing everybody else to miss their breakfast; selfish pricks. Poor Hugh's sick now, too; I just hope it's his seasonal allergies, and not that bug he's got. I'm going to try to get some shut eye. So damn anxious, though. This is going to be a long night. I hope this whole clusterfuck doesn't make me miss my court date.

Hey shit head. You know you who are. It's me, Bill Benson. Remember how we promised each other, that we'd ride this out together? That we'd have each other's backs no matter what, and we'd never abandon one another regardless of how fucking bad it got, no matter how terrifying the situation?

You lied.

You know exactly what you fucking did. You thought you could make off with ALL of our food, all of MY fucking ammo-- you didn't do ANY of the fucking preparation, "roomie". You always tried to poke fun at me, make me out like I was paranoid, even fucking called the cops because you were so fucking scared shitless that I was exercising my right to keep and bear arms. Lo and fucking behold, the dead walk the earth, yea the apocalypse is nigh, and you think you can just take all my shit, cut and run? After I taught you to shoot, after I bared my heart and soul to you, after the things we did together? You think you can just fucking GET AWAY with it?

You are unbelievably stupid. You fired off a shot, knowing damn well it'd bring a herd of those fuckers down onto the apartment, and you stole my god damn truck, and now I'm getting REALLY close to finding you. I will stop at absolutely nothing, I will hunt you to the end of the earth and make you walk with them. I'll blow your fucking guts out, and leave you to turn.

Keep running, because that only makes this more fun.

Bill

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_49_Content:
The nasty girls are shooting on sight now. They're not even bothering to hide it anymore, anyone trying to leave, or trying to enter, gets shot dead. Used to be they'd just arrest you, quarantine you then let you go into the city to evac, that's what my sister said on the radio before she and a few dozen others got ferried across the river into Indiana.

I write this letter to anybody who might find it from my deathbed. Me and my cousin Jesse tried to approach the gate, wanting to get in, to evacuate like everyone else, but the moment we came into sight, they killed Jesse, blew his brains out all over the concrete with an M16, and then they popped me a few times.

I managed to get away, to get back to my car, but I'm losing blood just steady enough that I've got maybe twenty minutes left as I write this. My last will and testament to whoever comes across this letter, praying it hasn't been soaked through:

You can have all my gear. I won't be needing it. If you're able and willing, try to get to Indianapolis, that's where they took my sister Vivian. Give her this note, so she's not left in the dark.

I love you Viv.

Mitchell

This new world without you is starting and the old world is ending, I am going go to live on to see and feel the sunlight of another day so that the life you had sacrificed for me would be worth something.

I've missed you so much, Jim...
I will make it worth your life.

A month and week passed... In the evening summer as I was drinking to forget the reality I can't forget about that day on how it take his life forever, away from my life. It got me thinking and pushed myself to find him once again, it was the Riverside church... went back there and it was quiet and beautiful as usual apart from a wall of blood that I painted red.

That day, we fled out of the church and went into one of the houses, he was holding the door but then it broke down before... they mauled him alive, I could only run away and don't look back. Now I am here again in the house where I last saw him, there is a pile of blood, guts, and flesh all around but no sign of him but a trail of blood that leads to the backyard of the house. I followed the trail as what've his remains started to appear more and more and eventually, his hand with still a wedding ring on it... the same one as mine, as I was looking down at it I heard weird knocking sounds behind a woods and hoping to myself that it would be him and when I see it... I can't believe my own eyes.

It was my husband, Jim. With his half, the bottom of his body from his stomach was torn off, both of his hands as well, and one missing eyeball. Still in that black suit like on that wedding day, bloodied and muddied... beyond recognizable but I know it is him.
I- I can't hold myself back from this and not breaks into tears and collapse down, looking at him as he tried to reach out for me to take a bite but he was in a bad shape that he can't even crawl to me.
In the end, I finished him and set him free from this pain... for ever.

I brought what's left of his body back afterward to a proper burial, now his grave won't be empty anymore...
I've found you.

After the burial that night, I even dreamed about him, about the world without the infection where we live happily but it was just a fantasy...

Ever since the commies gave up, I've known it was only a matter of time for something else to come along. Another joke on us. Something else to fight, something else to kill. And here it is. Inside us. Turning us on each other. Making US into THEM. Well I'm not going that way. I'm on my own road, I'm at the wheel of this life. I've got everything I need right here, and I'm going to need it all to get where I'm going. Anyone finds this, good luck to you if you're a red-blooded American survivor, but if you're one of them, Johnson Dukakis says f!ck you.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_84_Content: If you're here for the same reason I am, don't f!cking bother. Some assh!le already took all the K. What the hell's that all about, man? That's not copascetic. Just leaving damn xyla for the rest of us. Stuff'll kill you and won't give you a good high no matter what you're jamming to. Just a douche move. I'm out and you probly should be, too. Place ain't safe. Peace.

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_88_Content:
THE TRUTH OF THE MATTER
I, Mandy Potemkin, am going to kill all of my coworkers and then myself on 7/8/93. I do not intend to do this out of hatred for them, as they are my friends and have done no wrong but what they have been forced to, as I will now. I am not of unsound mind and do not do this out of something as foolish as momentary passion or as worthless as monetary debt. No, I do this to prove to the world the truth of the matter, that we are all victims of a system and government which do not care for us. Our lives have such little worth to our capitalist and authoritarian rulers that we might as well be mindless drones, marching ever onwards, only consuming, never creating. But I believe by killing myself and my friends, I may not only save us from suffering any longer into this worthless future, but too damage the machinations of our seemingly untouchable overlords and prove to others like us that we can make a difference if only we act and react with haste and with force. This is the truth of the matter, that violence must be done.

I plan to enact my plan first by:
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_89_Content:
*Two anime-style characters with swords stand in opposition, captioned.*

"This is the end for you Lucifer! I have the power of my forebears behind me and they have blessed my sword with power you could never comprehend! Surender now and I'll show you something you never could show my family. Mercy!"
"It ain't nothing personnal, Kriss-X, but as you are the daughter of the Gemstone King, I am sworn to fulfill my destiny and end your empire, freeing the people forever. Lay down the Lightblade and I will make it quick."
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_8_Content:
3 Months later... How long can I keep going? I ask myself this question every dawn and sunset as I am uncertain about the current life I am having. I woke up, I go kill those rotten walking corpses, I live and repeat. It seems like I have no goals in my life but to keep living for him that... Does it still worth it? Do I make him proud of me? Or I should be the one who's up there instead... Maybe I died on the same day as you on our wedding day just so I can see and you stay with me forever. 

I am not sure but I started to hear some voices lately, but it was just me and no one else. Was that your voice calling me when I don't wanna keep going? Was that you that always calm me down when I want to end my own life?
*Am I going insane?*

The feelings of anxiety and loneliness are slowly breaking through the cracks like poison in my bone. Sometimes I am not sure which sounds is real anymore... but his voice always comforts me and it keeps me going, although how can I keep going like this?
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_8_Title: Natalie's Journal - Act VI: Voices from you
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_90_Content: There are better ways to kill yourself. Don't eat any of this stuff unless you want them to hear your colon exploding and come swarm you as the salmon takes its revenge. I know it looks good, but you're worth more than a bite of sushi. Try the river if you're really hurting for some fish and shrimp. Might see you there. Good luck.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_91_Content: Chris, we are NOT going to JPG! Even if we could get across the bridges (because not all of us can swim, Chris!) into Indiana, do you know how crazy it is to try to get into ANY military base? You should just try walking right into Fort Knox! I get that JPG seemed all nice and peaceful when we went there as kids, but this isn't a field trip, and nobody (not even the soldiers) know where not to step in that place to not get blown into tiny chunks. Hell, the entire range might be freaking radioactive! Listen, dude, we just need to find somewhere quiet to wait this whole thing out, and it doesn't need to be 100 miles away in an old bomb test site, alright? We're over at Michelle's if you want to hang out, but leave this at home, OK? Love you.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_92_Content: A farmer looked over his crops and saw they were wilting for there had been no rain for a week. He went to the hill and asked of the highest powers to bring rain so that those who depended on him would not know hunger. And the rains came and stayed for two weeks, tearing down an immense oak which grew over the farmer's home and smashed it all. He again went to the hill and cursed the rain, demanding for it to stop. And so the rain stopped and returned the sun, endless and blazing, for two months, burning the farmer's crop and stripping the whole land of life. He returned to the hill and with parched lips begged only for shade. And the sunset arrived only for sunrise to never come, leaving the world dark. Unable to see, the farmer could not find the hill again, and so all creation was plunged into lifeless darkness forever.

UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_94_Content:
Liz, a guy came in with a freaky order that I need your help with, also figured you might get a kick out of it. So here this guy is, decked out in full hunting gear, like, y'know, camo everything, fake leaves, face paint that makes him look like a baby barfed on his face, and he asks for all the books and mags we can get on - wait for it - farming. Wants anything about digging in dirt and watering plants going all the way back to 1776. Said he knew everything he needed to about everything else - no sh!t - but couldn't tell a potato from a pumpkin except that one's served with your Spiffo's #1 and the other's in his nana's Thanksgiving pie. What a character, right?

Anyway, I can get all that stuff for him. But then he asked for - and you knew it was coming - every issue of HottieZ going back to 1965. Said anything older makes him feel like he's perving on his mom. I figure your girl in Nashville's gotta have a supply of them, and I bet this guy isn't going to be picky if they're repros or microfiche dupes, so if you can work that angle, be my guest. Man, people are getting weird out there, huh?

See you Monday!
Larry
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_95_Content: Burn everything. Evac AO. Liquidation beginning 03:00.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_96_Content:
7-8-93
Got back from a run to the farmer's market (almost got into a fight with some roadrager in a Rancher, people are starting to lose it) just to find the door busted open. Some jackass looter broke in and wrecked the place. But that's all it looks like he did, cause as far as I can tell nothing's missing. What the hell? Guess I know what I'm doing for the rest of the evening.

OK. Strike that. The guy did take some stuff, but just my floppies. Pulled every one out of the bins and even the DOS copy out of the drive. Now if I could just figure out why. I guess some people do have weird klepto fetishes, but old disks never would cross my mind. Hope he likes playing GRIM and reading BBS convos from five years ago. Just strange.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_97_Content: I'm not making it down to the Lower Depths, looks like, so I'll just sit here and write. Put it out there into the night air. Conway better be taking care of Lysette, not that I don't expect him to. He's shaped up a lot since he quit the liquor, and she's needed him to since her mind's been going. Hardest thing he's ever done, I'd wager, sobering up just to sit and watch her slip into the dark. Might be a kindness on the part of God, honestly, her forgetting, ever since Charlie and Ira. Might be the wrath of Him that Conway's got to sit and be the only one to remember between the two. Can't ever repay that debt he thinks Lysette's owed. I pity the old guy.\n\nJunebug and Johnny came through a week or so before they put up the border. She seemed to know there was something coming, like she always does, seeing things before and after they've happened. Wish I'd gone with them, though it's not like I'd fit in the sidecar between Johnny, their gear, and that beautiful old dress. They were going to the bar for a gig and we'd all have been there days before the camo guys rolled in. Probably halfway to Santiago by now, riding hard through the nights, gas needle always on zero. Or maybe they're holding out in that old mine they used to hang around. Envy them that, being young and able. Suppose that's my late reflection, hah hah.
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_98_Content:
Daryl,
So here's what me and Marty figured out. The army's got all the airfields locked down but they ain't watching any of the dirt strips right? Well we're gonna get the old cropduster out of the barn and roll it down to Sally's to try and see if she'll help us get it flying again. Then we'll all jump in and take off for the Keys. How's that sound huh? It worked in Nam right? And it ain't like they'll scramble to shootdown some little duster flying around. So if you wanna join in we're gonna be starting the roll on Tueday and heading down Old Mill toward Lickskillet. We sure could use your help and I'd get Marty to let you set up front.
Your pal,
Ronnie
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_99_Content: July 7, 1993\nSome f!cker BIT ME today! Like, what the sh!t, dude!? He came stumbling up like he was high or something, and when he was just standing there staring at me, I asked if he was OK, and then he, like, fell over on me and totally BIT ME! Rocky got him off me, and the guy was just flopping around on the sidewalk after that, so maybe he was totally high, but, like, dude!? He bit me so hard, and now I'm all messed up! Hope he liked the taste of f!cking silicone! So Rocky's taking me to the doc tomorrow to get some antibiotics or whatever, make sure it's not infected, and maybe fix the damage. He's so sweet. Maybe I'll pick out a new blouse, too! Tomorrow's going to be great!
UI_ImmersiveLore_Story_9_Content: I never thought I'd miss Mondays, but here we are, in the middle of the zombie apocalypse. It's strange how the little things we took for granted become the things we yearn for the most. I miss the sound of the alarm clock, the rush to get ready for work, and even the annoying morning traffic.\n\nThose mundane routines gave our lives a sense of purpose and normalcy. Now, every day feels like a battle for survival. But I hold onto the hope that one day, Mondays will return, and we'll complain about them just like we used to.

UI_J93RunningBloodPools_BloodyFootstepsE: Wet tracked pools can contaminate a survivor's path. Multiplayer trail creation and placement are decided by the server.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_CorpseChance_Too: Percentage chance that an eligible newly killed zombie or enabled dead player corpse creates a pool. Multiplayer rolls are made only by the server.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_DebugMode_Toolti: Writes persistence, migration, growth, native blood fallback, and synchronization diagnostics to console.txt. Leave off during normal play.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_Description: Single-player uses these values locally. In multiplayer, the server's Sandbox settings are authoritative for shared pools, drying, rain washing, and bloody trails; only Debug Logging remains client-local.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_Enabled_Tooltip: Master switch for newly created persistent pools and their bloody footprint trails.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_FootprintDryDays: In-game days until ordinary age-based wetness reaches zero. Rain can reduce wetness much faster. Visual thinning has its own toggle and configurable minimum stain.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_FootstepCount_To: Maximum marks from a fully wet pool. The count scales down automatically as the source pool dries.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_FootstepSpacing_: Travel distance required between bloody marks. Smaller values create a tighter, denser trail.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_GrowthSteps_Tool: Number of deterministic outward growth stages stored with the pool. Higher values look smoother and create more decals.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_MaximumRadius_To: Maximum distance from the pool center. Each created pool stores its chosen geometry for persistence and multiplayer reconstruction.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_MinimumDriedStai: Ordinary time-based drying will never thin a pool below this percentage of its original deterministic deposits. Rain and vanilla blood cleanup can still remove more.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_PlayerCorpsePool: Newly dead player corpses can create the same persistent pools as zombie corpses. Uses the same chance and all normal growth, aging, rain, cleaning, and footprint rules.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_PoolAgingEnabled: Controls world-age wetness loss. When enabled, pools gradually stop transferring blood to shoes. Visual thinning is controlled separately.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_PoolGoreMultipli: Multiplies pool blood output. 1.20 is the intended default, 1.00 is baseline, and 3.00 is the experimental maximum.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_RainFootprintWas: How much faster thin bloody footprints wash away than dense pools. Default 3.0 means footprints need about one-third as much rain exposure.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_RainWashEnabled_: Rain physically erodes persistent pools that are outside and exposed to weather. Rain also rapidly reduces wetness. Indoor pools are protected.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_RainWashHours: Heavy Rain Hours to Wash Pool
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_RainWashHours_To: Equivalent hours of full-strength rain needed to completely wash away an exposed pool. Lighter rain accumulates proportionally more slowly.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_RainWashMinimumI: Rain weaker than this normalized intensity is ignored for washing. 0.10 allows light rain; higher values require stronger weather.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_RainWashesFootpr: Persistent outdoor bloody footprints are washed away by rain independently from their source pool.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_SplatsPerStep_To: Base deterministic deposits added per growth step. Increase this when using very large radii so the pool stays dense.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_SpreadDurationSe: How long each pool takes to finish spreading while loaded. Interrupted progress resumes from its persisted growth step.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_VisualAgingEnabl: Controls edge-to-center visual thinning separately from wetness. Disable this to keep pools visually full while world-age wetness can still decline.
UI_J93RunningBloodPools_ZombieBloodyFoot: Zombies that cross a wet tracked pool can leave persistent bloody footprints as they move away. Uses the same count, spacing, drying, cleaning, and rain-wash rules as survivor trails.

UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALEB_GREETING: Hello, I am Caleb Raines, a scout with the Drifters. I travel roads, shortcuts, and places no reliable map still records. Tell me where you need to go; I can offer a less dangerous route, but not a safe one.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALEB_RAINES_GREETING: If you are looking for the easy road, you are late. If you need one that is still open, I may be able to help.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALEB_RAINES_OPTION_PRI: Why do you not work for a settlement?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALEB_RAINES_OPTION_SIT: What have you seen on the roads?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALEB_RAINES_OPTION_WAR: What should I avoid out there?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALEB_RAINES_PRINCIPLE: Because a route stops being safe when an authority decides it owns it. I share what I know with travelers who respect the road, not with anyone trying to charge for crossing it.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALEB_RAINES_SITUATION: Main roads attract hordes, patrols, and people waiting behind a disabled car. I work with rural lanes, small bridges, and trails that can still carry a caravan.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALEB_RAINES_WARNING: Houses that look too untouched and detours that look too obvious. If a place seems prepared to receive you, somebody probably prepared it.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALEB_WHO_ARE_YOU: I scout roads, bridges, and rural crossings. I remember where the hordes were yesterday and watch where they move today.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_AUTHORITY: Knox Authority wants records, permits, and obedience. We already saw what its institutions were worth when people needed help.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_AUTONOMY: We will share surpluses and defend our neighbors, but nobody in another town will decide that we must surrender our land or supplies.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_DORSEY_GREETING: You can speak, but promises carry less weight here than what someone does afterward.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_DORSEY_OPTION_PR: Why do you distrust Knox Authority?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_DORSEY_OPTION_SI: What does this community need now?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_DORSEY_OPTION_WA: What do you expect from an outsider?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_DORSEY_PRINCIPLE: Because they began by offering coordination and now speak of registries and requisitions. Institutions that abandoned these people do not regain authority by printing new forms.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_DORSEY_SITUATION: Stable food, hands that can repair, and neighbors who keep their word. I do not need another flag; I need a family to survive winter without surrendering its harvest for protection.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_DORSEY_WARNING: Ask before taking, honor agreements, and do not mistake our cooperation for obedience.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_GREETING: I am Calvin Dorsey, and I help keep this community free. We survive through our own work, not orders sent from far away. Tell me whether you came to contribute or to govern us.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_CALVIN_WHO_ARE_YOU: I represent the families in this settlement, not a government or some distant council. My obligation is to the people behind these defenses.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DANIEL_AUTHORITY_RELATI: I will cooperate with Knox Authority while its orders protect the population. An official seal does not turn a bad order into a good one.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DANIEL_BROOKS_GREETING: If you bring a problem, describe it clearly. If you bring an order, first tell me who will have to pay for it.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DANIEL_BROOKS_OPTION_PR: How far would you obey Knox Authority?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DANIEL_BROOKS_PRINCIPLE: As long as its orders remain defensive and reasonable. Discipline keeps a unit alive; blind obedience only makes it easier for someone else to choose who gets sacrificed.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DANIEL_BROOKS_SITUATION: People, evacuation routes, and positions that keep them alive. A perimeter is worthless if holding it means abandoning those it was meant to protect.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DANIEL_BROOKS_WARNING: It returns with everyone, reports what it saw, and does not turn every encounter into a show of force.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DANIEL_GREETING: Hold there. I am Captain Daniel Brooks, commander of this area's defenses. If you need protection, tell me who we are covering, what the threat is, and for how long.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DANIEL_OLD_GUARD: The Old Guard is not the Army. We are the people who still know how to organize a defense, hold a line, and pull civilians out of a lost area.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DANIEL_WHO_ARE_YOU: I was a reservist. Now I coordinate this detachment. My responsibility is to keep routes open and get the people under our protection to the next day alive.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DENISE_CARTER_GREETING: Speak slowly, begin with the location, and separate what you saw from what you were told.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DENISE_CARTER_OPTION_WA: When do you consider a report reliable?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DENISE_CARTER_PRINCIPLE: Because an urgent lie is still a lie. A bad broadcast can empty a safe shelter or divert the people who were going to rescue someone.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DENISE_CARTER_SITUATION: Horde warnings, blocked routes, and calls for help. I compare times, voices, and locations before using a frequency for something that may send a patrol into a trap.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DENISE_CARTER_WARNING: When two independent sources agree and at least one can explain how the information was obtained.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DENISE_GREETING: Hello, I am Denise Carter, a KnoxNet operator. I receive reports, verify information, and transmit warnings to anyone still listening. Give me a location and carefully separate what you saw from what you assume.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_DENISE_WHO_ARE_YOU: I was an emergency dispatcher. Now I organize reports and warnings so a useful transmission is not buried beneath panic.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EDDIE_GREETING: Welcome to the market. I am Eddie Sloan, and I organize stalls, trades, and debts for the Knox Workforce. Tell me whether you need goods, a place to sell, or an account settled.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EDDIE_SLOAN_GREETING: If you need something scarce, it may exist. If you need something cheap, you will have to settle for what nobody else wants.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EDDIE_SLOAN_OPTION_PRIN: Do you work with The Syndicate?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EDDIE_SLOAN_OPTION_SITU: How do you keep this market open?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EDDIE_SLOAN_PRINCIPLE: I work with suppliers. Some use names, some use intermediaries, and some prefer to leave neither. Ask me about the goods, not the rumors.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EDDIE_SLOAN_SITUATION: By matching what one workshop has in excess with what another lacks, recording debts, and keeping disputes from closing routes everyone needs.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EDDIE_SLOAN_WARNING: When one side needs to pretend it never happened. Those agreements always cost twice.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EDDIE_WHO_ARE_YOU: I organize markets, routes, and agreements between workshops. Trade will not rebuild the world, but it keeps the people who can do it working.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_ETHICS: Desperation does not turn a person into laboratory material. I will not conduct a trial without explaining its risks and obtaining consent.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_FOSTER_GREETING: Before anything else: if you are injured, tell me where, for how long, and what you used to treat it.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_FOSTER_OPTION_PR: What would you refuse to do in search of a cure?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_FOSTER_OPTION_SI: What is limiting the clinic now?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_FOSTER_PRINCIPLE: I will not turn desperation into consent. I will explain risks and alternatives even when that slows a study everyone wants finished.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_FOSTER_SITUATION: It is not only medicine. We lack beds, rested hands, and places to isolate someone without condemning them to abandonment. Every admission changes what we can treat tomorrow.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_FOSTER_WARNING: Antibiotics and anesthesia are obvious, but gloves, disinfectant, and clean records prevent more deaths than people imagine.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_GREETING: Hello, I am Doctor Elaine Foster, and I run the clinic in this area. If you are injured, tell me where and for how long. How can I help?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_INSTITUTE: The Institute is a network of clinics and specialists, not a single authority. We share procedures and results because withholding medical information costs lives.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_ELAINE_WHO_ARE_YOU: I was an emergency physician before the outbreak. Now I run this clinic, which means deciding every day what we can treat and what we must admit we cannot save.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EVELYN_GREETING: Hello. I am Evelyn Mercer, deputy director of emergency management for the Knox Authority. I coordinate resources, records, and agreements between settlements. Tell me what you need and what you can contribute.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EVELYN_KNOX_AUTHORITY: Knox Authority maintains records, coordinates convoys, and mediates between communities. Authority means nothing if it cannot protect people.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EVELYN_MERCER_GREETING: I have time for one concrete matter. Emergencies multiply when nobody decides what must be handled first.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EVELYN_MERCER_OPTION_SI: What is Knox Authority trying to build?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EVELYN_MERCER_OPTION_WA: What do you need for people to trust you?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EVELYN_MERCER_PRINCIPLE: When an emergency measure can no longer be reviewed, appealed, or ended. If we cannot explain an order, we probably should not impose it.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EVELYN_MERCER_SITUATION: An administration able to coordinate shelters, routes, and resources beyond a single street. Without continuity, every crisis forces us to begin from nothing.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EVELYN_MERCER_WARNING: Visible results, predictable rules, and the willingness to admit a mistake before burying it beneath another decree.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_EVELYN_WHO_ARE_YOU: Before the collapse, I was deputy director of emergency management. Now I am trying to keep every settlement from having to survive entirely alone.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_GERALD_GREETING: Good day. I am Gerald Haines, a former court clerk responsible for keeping our agreements from becoming rumors. Give me your name and the purpose of your visit; both will go on record.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_GERALD_HAINES_GREETING: Tell me what happened, who was present, and which part you can defend if someone disputes it.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_GERALD_HAINES_PRINCIPLE: It exists while we accept that a decision must be justified and that even those in command can be reviewed. Without that, only punishments with official stationery remain.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_GERALD_HAINES_SITUATION: Because decisions without memory become rumors, and rumors become excuses. An imperfect record still lets us ask who ordered a requisition and on what evidence.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_GERALD_HAINES_WARNING: Registers, deeds, medical files, and anything connecting names to decisions. Ordinary paper is more valuable than it looks.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_GERALD_WHO_ARE_YOU: I was a court clerk. Now I record decisions, property, requisitions, and disputes. Someone must preserve a verifiable memory of what we do.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_GERALD_WHY_RECORDS: Because abandoning records means abandoning accountability. Without evidence, every promise can be denied and every abuse can be justified.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HAROLD_GREETING: I am Doctor Harold Keene, an infectious-disease researcher with the Institute. If you brought a sample, leave it sealed on that tray; if you want answers, tell me exactly what you observed.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HAROLD_KEENE_GREETING: If you brought a sample, do not open it here. If you brought a question, choose carefully how much you want to know.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HAROLD_KEENE_OPTION_PRI: What do you know about Directive Twelve?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HAROLD_KEENE_PRINCIPLE: I recognize associated codes and protocols. That does not mean I ran the program, but some of its research predates what happened here.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HAROLD_KEENE_SITUATION: Transmission patterns, immune responses, and records from before the outbreak. Similarities matter less than differences between patients exposed in the same way.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HAROLD_KEENE_WARNING: Because an incomplete file can be dangerous in the hands of someone who already decided what it must prove. I verify the context first.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HAROLD_WHO_ARE_YOU: I research infectious diseases. I recognize some codes from before the outbreak, although that does not mean I have every answer.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HOLLIS_GREETING: I do not need your name yet. I need to know whether what you bring can be verified.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HOLLIS_OPTION_SITUATION: What kind of information do you buy?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HOLLIS_OPTION_WARNING: What do you know about Directive Twelve?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HOLLIS_PRINCIPLE: It is the name you need for this conversation. Knowing more would not make your information or my answer safer.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HOLLIS_SITUATION: Routes, documents, identities, and facts someone would prefer to keep separate. A rumor is worth little; a verifiable connection changes decisions.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HOLLIS_WARNING: Enough to recognize when someone found a real piece and when they are repeating words heard over the radio. Complete pieces cost more than money.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_HOLLIS_WHO_ARE_YOU: I listen, compare accounts, and decide what information deserves to circulate. Knowing something is useless if nobody trusts the source.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JESSE_CROWE_GREETING: Look at what you need, but point nothing toward me and do not ask where it came from.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JESSE_CROWE_OPTION_PRIN: What line will you not cross?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JESSE_CROWE_OPTION_SITU: Who are you willing to sell to?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JESSE_CROWE_OPTION_WARN: What should I check before buying?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JESSE_CROWE_PRINCIPLE: I do not arm people who shoot at shelters to demonstrate power. It is not morality; it is keeping the business from turning every road into a grave.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JESSE_CROWE_SITUATION: Anyone who can pay and understands that a weapon also buys responsibilities. There are clients I refuse even when their money is good.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JESSE_CROWE_WARNING: Compatible ammunition, magazines, worn parts, and who else knows you carry the weapon. The last one is usually the most dangerous.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JESSE_GREETING: I am Jesse Crowe, and I obtain weapons and supplies for anyone who can pay. Look all you want, do not touch what you cannot afford, and tell me what you need without asking where it came from.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JESSE_WHO_ARE_YOU: I move weapons and supplies along routes others prefer to ignore. The merchandise works. Explanations cost extra.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_COMMUNITY: New Knox Community does not exist in one place. It is families and settlements that keep communicating even when the roads try to separate them.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_GREETING: Hello, I am June Walker. I teach when I can and carry messages between communities when the roads allow it. If you have a letter or need news, give me a name, a destination, and who may know its contents.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_ROUTES: Routes change every week. A blocked bridge, a horde, or a patrol can turn a short trip into two days on the road.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_WALKER_GREETING: If you came from another community, tell me which one and when you left. News grows stale faster than bread.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_WALKER_OPTION_PRIN: How do you choose a route?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_WALKER_OPTION_SITU: What do you carry between settlements?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_WALKER_PRINCIPLE: By the hour, weather, possible shelters, and who controls each crossing. The shortest road is rarely the one that lets you return.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_WALKER_SITUATION: Agreements, requests for help, names of the missing, and news that should not be trusted to an open radio. I also remember who kept their word.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_WALKER_WARNING: Promises made in its name by people who never intend to keep them. A voluntary alliance only works when each community answers for what it offers.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_JUNE_WHO_ARE_YOU: I used to teach at a school. Now I carry letters, warnings, and news between communities that cannot always speak over the radio.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_CRUEL_ORDERS: An order that wastes lives for pride does not deserve blind obedience. Discipline does not mean you stop thinking.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_EVACUATION: This center receives families, wounded people, and the displaced. The hospital takes serious cases, but the routes change every hour.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_GREETING: Hello, I am Sergeant Lena Ortiz. I organize shelters, evacuations, and rescues for the Old Guard. If someone is in danger, give me a location and a possible route; if you need a roof, say so plainly.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_ORTIZ_GREETING: If this is an emergency, give me the number of people, location, and last contact.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_ORTIZ_OPTION_PRINC: When would you disobey an order?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_ORTIZ_OPTION_SITUA: How do you organize an evacuation?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_ORTIZ_OPTION_WARNI: What is the most common rescue mistake?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_ORTIZ_PRINCIPLE: When it has no defensive purpose and its cost is lives surrendered for pride. I will say so aloud before I do it.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_ORTIZ_SITUATION: First an exit route, then transport, assembly points, and someone counting people. Running without a destination only scatters survivors.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_ORTIZ_WARNING: Sending more people without understanding why the first group became trapped. Courage does not replace information.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_LENA_WHO_ARE_YOU: I coordinate security and evacuations. Getting someone out alive matters more than planting a flag over an empty building.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MAE_GREETING: Careful with that table. I am Mae Turner, a carpenter and electrician with the Knox Workforce. I keep buildings standing and their lights on. What do you need built or repaired?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MAE_TURNER_GREETING: If something stopped working, tell me what it did immediately before. If it never worked, we have a different problem.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MAE_TURNER_OPTION_PRINC: What do you think of large projects?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MAE_TURNER_OPTION_WARNI: Which materials are never in excess?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MAE_TURNER_PRINCIPLE: They work if we can maintain them with local tools. An impressive facility depending on an irreplaceable part is only a delayed ruin.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MAE_TURNER_SITUATION: The one preventing us from losing water, power, or a roof before the next storm. Pretty improvements can wait; failure points cannot.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MAE_TURNER_WARNING: Nails, wire, fuses, dry lumber, and parts that can be adapted. Also people who return a tool when they finish.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MAE_WHO_ARE_YOU: I work with wood and electricity. A sturdy wall is not much use if you cannot light it, heat it, or connect an alarm.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_CODES: I learned them during continuity-of-government exercises. Forms, evacuation routes, warehouse designations. Nothing useful without the rest of the protocol.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_GREETING: Hello, I am Malcolm Reed, and I coordinate logistics for the Knox Authority. If you need fuel, transport, or supplies, tell me what cargo you are moving and which route you intend to use.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_LOGISTICS: Logistics decides who eats, which generator stays running, and which community receives help before the road closes.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_REED_GREETING: I need origin, destination, volume, and date. Without those, it is not logistics; it is a wish.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_REED_OPTION_PRI: Where did you learn those codes?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_REED_OPTION_SIT: What are you trying to supply?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_REED_PRINCIPLE: From continuity exercises and manuals almost nobody read when they still seemed hypothetical. The rest does not change what opens a door.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_REED_SITUATION: Posts, shelters, and convoys consuming resources at different rates. My work is keeping an unmoving reserve from looking like abundance while another position runs empty.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_REED_WARNING: Predictable schedules, manifests that are too public, and people who think an escort replaces an alternate route.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MALCOLM_WHO_ARE_YOU: I coordinate warehouses, vehicles, and convoys for Knox Authority. A crate in the wrong place helps nobody, even when it is full of medicine.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARA_BELL_GREETING: I can find a door when every other one is closed. The question is what you will accept owing afterward.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARA_BELL_OPTION_PRINCI: Who do you really work for?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARA_BELL_OPTION_SITUAT: What kind of agreements do you negotiate?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARA_BELL_OPTION_WARNIN: What is the risk of accepting your help?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARA_BELL_PRINCIPLE: For the continuity of my agreements. Factions change leaders and principles; a well-recorded debt survives both.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARA_BELL_SITUATION: Access, goods, information, and favors between people who cannot meet without starting a war. I make the exchange possible and remember its cost.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARA_BELL_WARNING: Solving today’s problem with an obligation you cannot ignore tomorrow. I never hide that there will be a price, only when it will be collected.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARA_GREETING: I am Mara Bell, a broker for the Syndicate. I find people, goods, and arrangements others prefer not to advertise. Before telling me what you seek, tell me what you can offer and who knows you came.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARA_WHO_ARE_YOU: I connect needs with opportunities. Names, routes, and motives belong to whoever can pay for them.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARTIN_GREETING: They call me Sparks Webb. I am a KnoxNet radio technician, and I keep communications open between settlements. If your equipment hums, whistles, or catches fire, let me see it and tell me when it started.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARTIN_WEBB_GREETING: Lower your voice for a moment. I am following a weak signal and almost have the words separated from the noise.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARTIN_WEBB_OPTION_SITU: Which link are you trying to maintain?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARTIN_WEBB_PRINCIPLE: Because a warning kept as strategic leverage reaches the people who needed it too late. I verify what I can, but I do not bury useful news.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARTIN_WEBB_SITUATION: The repeaters between Muldraugh and West Point. Every failed segment leaves entire communities dependent on couriers and rumors.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARTIN_WEBB_WARNING: Dry batteries, clean connections, a well-placed antenna, and someone willing to listen even when no answer is expected.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_MARTIN_WHO_ARE_YOU: I build and repair transmitters. KnoxNet exists because there are still people willing to keep a frequency open.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_ADAPTATION: Veterinary medicine has always dealt with patients of different sizes, metabolisms, and anatomies. Adapting does not mean guessing. It means measuring, observing, and correcting.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_COLE_GREETING: Keep the sample sealed and tell me whether it came from a person, an animal, or the environment. That detail changes everything.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_COLE_OPTION_PRINCI: Why do some physicians question you?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_COLE_OPTION_SITUAT: What do you contribute to a human clinic?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_COLE_OPTION_WARNIN: What pattern are you looking for?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_COLE_PRINCIPLE: Because they confuse specialty with limitation. Then they call when equipment must be adapted or a sample does not fit their manuals.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_COLE_SITUATION: Adaptable procedures, microbiology, and experience working without equipment designed for the exact patient. Anatomy changes; contamination does not ask for credentials.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_COLE_WARNING: Differences between exposure, symptoms, and inflammatory response. Animals can also reveal which part of the environment is carrying a risk.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_GREETING: Hello, I am Doctor Nina Cole, a veterinarian and microbiologist with the Institute. I adapt equipment and treatments for any patient still breathing. Tell me what is wrong, and we will see what we can work with.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_MICROBIOLOGY: I can study samples and recognize patterns, but this is not a complete laboratory. A rushed conclusion can be more dangerous than having none.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NINA_WHO_ARE_YOU: I am a veterinarian and I studied microbiology. Before the outbreak I treated animals; now I adapt equipment and procedures for any patient still breathing.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NORA_GREETING: Hello, I am Nora Shaw, a traveling nurse and trader with the Drifters. I can examine that wound or show you what I carry in the wagon. Tell me which you need more urgently.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NORA_SHAW_GREETING: I have food, maps, and some medicine. I also have limits: if the wound is deep, I will not pretend to be a clinic.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NORA_SHAW_OPTION_PRINCI: Why do you not stay with The Institute?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NORA_SHAW_OPTION_SITUAT: What do you find during your travels?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NORA_SHAW_PRINCIPLE: Because someone must bring help to those who will never reach a clinic. I prefer moving and knowing when a problem exceeds what I can treat.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NORA_SHAW_SITUATION: Communities with small surpluses, roads changing every week, and people needing treatment before they can reach a physician.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NORA_SHAW_WARNING: Water, bandages, a map they can read, and enough room to abandon something when running matters more.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_NORA_WHO_ARE_YOU: I travel with caravans, trade supplies, and treat wounds when nobody better is available. I have learned to know my limits.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_AUTHORITY_RELATI: Do you answer to Knox Authority?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_CALVIN_AUTHORITY: Why do you reject Knox Authority?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_CODES: Where did you learn those codes?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_COMMUNITY_AUTONO: What does autonomy mean to you?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_ELAINE_ETHICS: Do you reject every experimental treatment?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_FEAR_AS_ORDER: Do you believe fear maintains order?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_JUNE_ROUTES: What do you know about the routes?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_NINA_ADAPTATION: Can you adapt treatments for humans?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_NINA_MICROBIOLOG: What can you discover from your samples?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_TRADE: I want to see your supplies.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OPTION_WHY_RECORDS: Why do you keep recording everything?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OWEN_GREETING: I am Owen Price, a field technician with KnoxNet. I service repeaters and keep the remaining towers connected. If you came by road, tell me which antennas you saw and what problems you encountered.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OWEN_PRICE_GREETING: If you bring a story, begin with the fact that does not change when you tell it a second time.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OWEN_PRICE_OPTION_PRINC: Do you exaggerate to keep an audience?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OWEN_PRICE_OPTION_SITUA: What are you trying to achieve with your broadcasts?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OWEN_PRICE_OPTION_WARNI: What should never be announced without evidence?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OWEN_PRICE_PRINCIPLE: Sometimes I arrange incomplete details into a message people can understand. Denise calls it exaggeration when the story moves faster than verification.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OWEN_PRICE_SITUATION: Help an isolated person understand the danger without feeling already condemned. The voice matters because panic also travels by radio.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OWEN_PRICE_WARNING: An evacuation, a cure, or the fall of a shelter. Those words make people abandon choices that could still save them.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_OWEN_WHO_ARE_YOU: I maintain relays, antennas, and power sources. A network depends less on one great station than on many small points that refuse to go dark.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_AUTHORITY_RELATI: What is your relationship with Knox Authority?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_CALVIN_AUTHORITY: What is your problem with Knox Authority?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_CODES: Those codes do not look regional.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_COMMUNITY_AGREEM: Can I trust the settlements in the alliance?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_COMMUNITY_AUTONO: How far does this community's independence go?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_CRUEL_ORDERS: What do you do if an order puts civilians at risk?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_ELAINE_ETHICS: What do you think about experimental treatments?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_ELAINE_TRADE: Can we trade supplies for the clinic?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_FEAR_AS_ORDER: Do you use fear to control people?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_JOBS: Do you need help with anything?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_JUNE_ROUTES: I need information about the roads.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_NEW_KNOX_COMMUNI: Tell me about New Knox Community.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_NINA_ADAPTATION: How do you adapt veterinary equipment and procedures?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_NINA_MICROBIOLOG: What do you know about the infection?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_OLD_GUARD: Tell me about the Old Guard.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_PRISONERS: I want to know what happened to the detainees.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_SAMUEL_MEDICINES: What medicines can The Institute produce?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_SAMUEL_SUBSTITUT: What can we use when the correct medicine is unavailable?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_TRADE: What do you have available for trade?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_WHO_ARE_YOU: I want to know who you are.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_PLAYER_WHY_RECORDS: Why do those records matter so much?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_RUTH_COLLINS_GREETING: If you represent a community, tell me what it can offer as well as what it needs. That is how honest agreements begin.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_RUTH_COLLINS_OPTION_WAR: How do you recognize a fair agreement?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_RUTH_COLLINS_PRINCIPLE: Those made in New Knox’s name by groups wanting protection but never contributing food, shelter, or people when another settlement needs them.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_RUTH_COLLINS_SITUATION: Clear exchanges, help that can be returned, and mediators who know each community’s real capacity. Goodwill without planning runs out.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_RUTH_COLLINS_WARNING: Neither side gets everything, both understand their obligations, and failure has consequences agreed before it happens.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_RUTH_COMMUNITY_AGREEMEN: Some use our name and never deliver what they promised. An agreement only matters if someone is willing to answer when winter arrives.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_RUTH_GREETING: Welcome. I am Ruth Collins, a farmer and mediator for the New Knox Community. If you need food, shelter, or a fair agreement, we will see what we can do for you.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_RUTH_NEW_KNOX_COMMUNITY: We are not a government. We are communities that chose to share enough to avoid disappearing separately.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_RUTH_WHO_ARE_YOU: I am a farmer. Mediating between settlements came from knowing the families and understanding what each farm could contribute.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_GREETING: Hello, I am Samuel Reed, a pharmacist with the Institute. I maintain the medicines we can still find or prepare. Before requesting treatment, tell me who it is for, their symptoms, and what else they are taking.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_MEDICINES: We can produce some basic medicines, but pure ingredients, sterile containers, and dosage control are becoming increasingly difficult to secure.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_REED_GREETING: Tell me the medicine, the dose, and who it is for. “Something strong” is not a prescription.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_REED_OPTION_PRIN: When would you accept a substitute?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_REED_OPTION_WARN: Which supplies do you need most urgently?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_REED_PRINCIPLE: When the likely benefit exceeds the risk and we can control the dose. Two substances looking alike does not mean the body treats them alike.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_REED_SITUATION: Basic preparations, disinfectants, and some substitutes when I know concentration, purity, and storage. Improvising without measurement only exchanges illness for poisoning.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_REED_WARNING: Sealed antibiotics, painkillers, alcohol, clean containers, and labels. Medicine without a name or date becomes a threat.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_SUBSTITUTES: A substitute is not automatically safe. Changing one substance or concentration can turn a reasonable treatment into poison.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SAMUEL_WHO_ARE_YOU: I am a pharmacist. I try to maintain a useful inventory and keep desperation from turning every unmarked bottle into a supposed cure.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SILAS_ASHFORD_GREETING: You are in my way, and I have not decided whether that is your bad luck or an opportunity for both of us.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SILAS_ASHFORD_OPTION_WA: Is there a way to cross without trouble?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SILAS_ASHFORD_PRINCIPLE: By taking what we need from those unable to defend it and leaving enough fear that the next group pays before arguing.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SILAS_ASHFORD_SITUATION: Because nobody can expel us from an organization without leaders. The name opens routes, confuses patrols, and forces other travelers to explain they are not like us.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SILAS_ASHFORD_WARNING: Yes. Make the price of letting you pass greater than the profit from taking everything. Do the calculation carefully.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SILAS_GREETING: I am Silas Ashford, and this caravan answers to me. I keep my people fed and moving, and nobody here lives on promises. Tell me what you can do and why I should listen.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_SILAS_WHO_ARE_YOU: I keep my people alive by taking what we need before somebody else does. You can call it violence. I call it reaching tomorrow.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_TRACKER_EXPLANATION: It is a modular Tracking Device. Compatible extensions can use it to track missions, mark areas and destinations, display objectives and progress and guide you to contacts. It costs ${price}.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_TRACKER_INSUFFICIENT: You do not have enough money. The device costs ${price}.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_TRACKER_PLAYER_OFFER: What is that device you are carrying?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_TRACKER_PLAYER_PURCHASE: All right. I'll take it for ${price}.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_TRACKER_PURCHASED: Done. It is yours. Compatible extensions will enable its functions through their respective interfaces.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WALTER_BRIGGS_GREETING: If that engine made a new noise, shut it down. If it stopped making an old noise, shut it down faster.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WALTER_BRIGGS_OPTION_WA: Which spare parts are worth keeping?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WALTER_BRIGGS_PRINCIPLE: Because whoever signs an order never returns the wrench they took or replaces the part they broke. I prefer agreements with one responsible person.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WALTER_BRIGGS_SITUATION: Vehicles, generators, and machines surviving on incompatible parts, frequent adjustments, and more wire than I would admit to another mechanic.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WALTER_BRIGGS_WARNING: Belts, hoses, spark plugs, filters, bearings, and any small part capable of stopping a large machine.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WALTER_GREETING: Hello, I am Walt Briggs, a mechanic with the Knox Workforce. If it has an engine, wheels, or makes a noise it should not, I can inspect it. Tell me what broke and which parts you have.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WALTER_WHO_ARE_YOU: I am a mechanic. I keep vehicles and generators running with parts that should already be in a scrapyard.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_FEAR_AS_ORDER: Fear keeps people behind barricades, away from restricted areas, and attentive to orders. Properly managed, it saves lives.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_GREETING: Stop there. I am Warren Pike, and I guard this checkpoint. You are inside a protected area, so tell me who you are, where you came from, and what brings you here.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_PIKE_GREETING: Keep your hands visible and answer directly. Confusion here lasts until someone gets hurt.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_PIKE_OPTION_PRIN: Do you not fear becoming what you fight?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_PIKE_OPTION_SITU: What kind of order do you enforce?
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_PIKE_PRINCIPLE: I fear more a settlement discovering too late that its rules were suggestions. Authority that hesitates invites others to decide for it.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_PIKE_SITUATION: Visible patrols, firm perimeters, and consequences nobody can pretend not to understand. Properly directed fear keeps a threat from testing our limits.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_PIKE_WARNING: They are registered, questioned, and held while they remain a risk. Compassion does not require returning a weapon to someone who already used it against us.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_PRISONERS: The detainees were processed according to the situation. If you are looking for a specific name, present a better reason than curiosity.
UI_KCMAIN_DIALOG_WARREN_WHO_ARE_YOU: I was a sheriff's deputy. Now I keep this sector under control while others waste time arguing over who has authority.
UI_KCMAIN_FACTION_DRIFTERS_DESCRIPTION: The Drifters are not a single organization, but the name given to caravans, refugees, scouts, and traders who live in motion. They share knowledge of the roads, distrust of borders, and the certainty that no shelter is permanent. Each caravan chooses its own leadership: some follow experienced scouts, others decide by council, while violent groups obey whoever controls food, vehicles, or weapons. They seek fuel, news, clear routes, safe camps, and lightweight goods for trade. Informal customs protect campsites, messengers, and water sources, but no authority can enforce them. Their ranks include rescuers, opportunists, and raiders. To a settlement, a Drifter band may bring the first news from the outside world or become the threat arriving before dawn.
UI_KCMAIN_FACTION_INSTITUTE_DESCRIPTION: The Institute is a network of clinics, improvised laboratories, and specialists sharing knowledge so medicine does not disappear. Its immediate motivation is saving lives; its long-term goal is understanding the infection, preserving reproducible treatments, and training new medical personnel. Each site manages its daily resources, while a clinical council of physicians, pharmacists, veterinarians, and technicians establishes protocols and distributes scarce samples, instruments, and drugs. In an emergency, the professional responsible for the patient commands, not whoever holds the highest political rank. The Institute values verifiable data, sterility, consent, and continuous records. Scarcity nevertheless creates conflict between treating today's patients, reserving resources for future outbreaks, and permitting experimental research that might save thousands or sacrifice people who could still be saved.
UI_KCMAIN_FACTION_KNOXNET_DESCRIPTION: KnoxNet is a decentralized network of operators, radio enthusiasts, and technicians dedicated to keeping settlements from becoming isolated. It maintains repeaters, listening schedules, horde warnings, weather reports, and links for rescue or trade. No station controls the entire network: each node remains autonomous, while veteran operators agree on frequencies, codes, and standards for verifying reports. During a crisis, authority temporarily rests with whoever has the most reliable information or the link to the affected area. KnoxNet protects batteries, electronic components, towers, and relay locations, but considers credibility its most valuable resource. It tries to remain neutral so everyone keeps listening. That neutrality is tested whenever a transmission could save lives, expose a hidden shelter, or become a weapon of propaganda.
UI_KCMAIN_FACTION_KNOX_AUTHORITY_DESCRIP: The Knox Authority intends to rebuild a civil government capable of surviving the disaster. Its priorities are registering survivors, protecting archives, coordinating convoys, settling disputes, and restoring basic services. A provisional council of former officials and local delegates leads it; departments manage their own specialties, while emergency decisions fall to an executive directorate. Its power depends less on weapons than on maps, permits, warehouses, and records of debts and property. It offers stability in exchange for cooperation, taxes, and obedience to common rules. The Authority contains both idealists determined to preserve civil rights and administrators convinced that, without central control, Knox will fracture into territories ruled by local strongmen.
UI_KCMAIN_FACTION_KNOX_WORKFORCE_DESCRIP: Knox Workforce brings together workshops, builders, mechanics, electricians, haulers, and market organizers. It believes survival depends on maintaining the tools that turn a temporary shelter into a lasting community. Its interests include fuel, spare parts, construction materials, generators, vehicles, and secure trade routes. It is administered as a federation of crews and workshops: supervisors calculate costs and needs, while a council of master tradespeople coordinates projects affecting the whole network. Authority is earned through proven skill and honored contracts, not titles held before the outbreak. They accept payment, barter, or future labor and record every debt. Their central dispute pits those who see infrastructure as a community service against those who argue that free work destroys the incentives keeping the network alive.
UI_KCMAIN_FACTION_NEW_KNOX_COMMUNITY_DES: New Knox Community is an alliance of farms, fortified neighborhoods, and rural shelters that chose mutual aid without creating a central government. It seeks to secure food, seed, water, shelter, and local defense while preserving each settlement's autonomy. Common decisions are negotiated in assemblies of delegates; spokespeople coordinate agreements but cannot impose them without the consent of affected families. Command changes with the need: farmers during planting, scouts on the roads, and defense leaders during attacks. Members exchange surpluses, labor, and shelter through promises enforced mainly by reputation. The alliance constantly debates whether closer cooperation is necessary or whether every distant authority is merely the beginning of another tyranny.
UI_KCMAIN_FACTION_OLD_GUARD_DESCRIPTION: The Old Guard is a defensive force formed by soldiers, reservists, police officers, firefighters, and trained civilians. Its stated mission is keeping routes open, evacuating populations, protecting shelters, and responding quickly to threats no community could face alone. It retains a military chain of command: commanders set objectives, officers direct sectors, and squads follow operational orders, although a council of veterans may challenge decisions that waste lives. It controls weapons, checkpoints, tactical vehicles, and disciplined personnel. That capacity makes it both a shield and a potential government in practice. Some members want to answer to restored civilian authority; others believe the emergency justifies martial law, requisitions, and permanent control. Its defining struggle is deciding when discipline protects the population and when it begins to rule it.
UI_KCMAIN_FACTION_SYNDICATE_DESCRIPTION: The Syndicate is a clandestine network of traders, smugglers, brokers, and informants thriving wherever laws and official routes fail. It pursues profit, influence, and access: restricted medicine, weapons, identities, secrets, and safe passage are worth more than currency. It has no public command. Separate cells, buyers, and brokers know only the portion of each deal they require, while the most reputable intermediaries coordinate agreements and settle debts. Credit, favors, and the fear of exclusion secure obedience. The Syndicate avoids open wars because commerce requires living customers, yet it readily manipulates scarcity or sells compromising information. Some consider it an indispensable market; others see an invisible power that turns every human need into an outstanding account.

UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_CALEB_RAINES_SUMMARY: Scout. He knows rural roads, isolated houses, and forest routes. He helps those who respect travelers and avoids committing himself to any settlement. He scouts back roads, bridges, isolated homes, and forest trails for The Drifters caravans. He keeps a mental record of horde movements and avoids routes too familiar to raiders or patrols. He helps respectful travelers but refuses to place his knowledge under the control of any permanent settlement or government.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_CALVIN_DORSEY_ROLE: Autonomist leader of New Knox Community
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_CALVIN_DORSEY_SUMMARY: Leader of a settlement near Riverside. He rejects all outside authority and believes Knox Authority is trying to rebuild the same institutions that abandoned the population. He governs a settlement near Riverside and jealously protects its land, supplies, and freedom to make its own decisions. He is willing to cooperate with neighboring communities but rejects mandatory registries, requisitions, and any authority that claims to speak for his people. His opposition to Knox Authority comes from both political conviction and the memory of institutions that failed during the crisis.

UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_DANIEL_BROOKS_SUMMARY: Former reservist. He maintains strict discipline but avoids sacrificing civilians for political objectives. He cooperates with Knox Authority as long as its orders seem reasonable. As an Old Guard captain, he coordinates defenses, patrols, and support operations without treating civilians as expendable resources. He believes in discipline, preparation, and a clear chain of command, although he reserves the right to refuse irresponsible political orders. His cooperation with Knox Authority depends on its operations retaining a defensive purpose.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_DEAN_HOLLOWAY_ROLE: Dean Holloway is a member of the Old Guard.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_DEAN_HOLLOWAY_SUMMARY: Dean Holloway is a member of the Old Guard and is responsible for armory security.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_DENISE_CARTER_SUMMARY: Former radio technician. She coordinates relay repairs and verifies reports before broadcasting them. She believes that one false story can kill more people than a horde. She coordinates the teams that repair relays and organizes the reports KnoxNet receives from different communities. She cross-checks locations, testimony, and times before authorizing a broadcast because she knows a false warning can divert rescue teams or cause panic. Her priority is keeping the network trustworthy, even when that means delaying news that others want to broadcast immediately.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_DIANA_ROURKE_ROLE: Diana Rourke is a member of the Old Guard.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_DIANA_ROURKE_SUMMARY: Diana Rourke is a member of the Old Guard and is responsible for scouting.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_DOUGLAS_KENT_ROLE: Douglas Kent is a member of KnoxNet.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_DOUGLAS_KENT_SUMMARY: Douglas Kent is a member of KnoxNet and is responsible for relay operation.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_EDDIE_SLOAN_SUMMARY: Market organizer. He is charming, practical, and far too good at finding hard-to-get goods. He denies any formal connection to The Syndicate. He organizes stalls, trade routes, inventories, and market rules for Knox Workforce. His ability to find scarce goods keeps many workshops operating, although it fuels rumors about clandestine contacts. He trades materials and supplies, records debts, and works to keep agreements functioning even between rival factions.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_ELAINE_FOSTER_ROLE: Emergency physician and director of an Institute clinic
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_ELAINE_FOSTER_SUMMARY: Emergency physician. She runs one of the main clinics. She refuses to experiment without consent, although every death makes that position harder to maintain. She runs a clinic for The Institute and organizes emergency care when medicines, beds, and staff are insufficient. She defends informed consent and refuses to treat desperation as permission to experiment on patients. Every preventable death tests her principles and increases pressure from researchers willing to accept risks she considers unjustifiable. She trades basic clinical supplies and recovers useful medical materials to keep emergency wards open, reserving the scarcest equipment for those who have proven their support for the network.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_ELI_MERCER_ROLE: Eli Mercer is a member of The Drifters.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_ELI_MERCER_SUMMARY: Eli Mercer is a member of The Drifters and is responsible for scouting.

UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_EMILY_VARGAS_SUMMARY: Emily Vargas is a member of KnoxNet and is responsible for radio repair.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_ETHAN_COLE_ROLE: Ethan Cole is a member of the Old Guard.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_ETHAN_COLE_SUMMARY: Ethan Cole is a member of the Old Guard and is responsible for driving and transport.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_EVELYN_MERCER_ROLE: Knox Authority deputy director of emergency management
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_EVELYN_MERCER_SUMMARY: Former deputy director of emergency management. She is pragmatic and knows Knox Authority will be recognized only if it proves it can protect the population. She is willing to negotiate but considers some form of central authority inevitable. After the collapse, she turned scattered emergency procedures into a regional administration capable of registering the population, distributing resources, and negotiating with other settlements. She judges every decision by its ability to preserve order in the long term and accepts compromises when they strengthen the legitimacy of Knox Authority. Her greatest struggle is preventing exceptional measures from becoming a permanent form of authoritarianism.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_FIONA_BRIGGS_ROLE: Fiona Briggs is a member of the Old Guard.

UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_GEORGE_TANNER_ROLE: George Tanner is a member of Knox Workforce.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_GEORGE_TANNER_SUMMARY: George Tanner is a member of Knox Workforce and is responsible for warehouse work.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_GERALD_HAINES_SUMMARY: Former court clerk. He insists on recording decisions, trials, and requisitions even when paper is scarce. He believes abandoning the law means accepting the end of civilization for good. Within Knox Authority, he preserves minutes, testimony, requisitions, and rulings so that decisions can be reviewed in the future. He believes even imperfect justice requires rules, evidence, and institutional memory. His insistence on documenting everything brings him into conflict with those who believe immediate survival justifies ignoring every procedure.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_GRACE_HOLLOWAY_ROLE: Grace Holloway is a member of The Drifters.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_GRACE_HOLLOWAY_SUMMAR: Grace Holloway is a member of The Drifters and is responsible for foraging.

UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_HANNAH_WHITAKER_ROLE: Hannah Whitaker is a member of New Knox Community.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_HANNAH_WHITAKER_SUMMA: Hannah Whitaker is a member of New Knox Community and is responsible for farming.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_HAROLD_KEENE_SUMMARY: Researcher specializing in infectious diseases. He has information about studies conducted before the outbreak. He denies taking part in government programs but recognizes codes associated with Directive Twelve. Within The Institute, he works with clinical records, samples, and references to pre-outbreak research. He recognizes terminology and codes connected to Directive Twelve but gives partial, carefully calculated explanations of their origin. His knowledge can guide the search for facilities and records, although it also suggests a deeper connection to former government programs.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_HELEN_WARD_ROLE: Helen Ward is a member of the Old Guard.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_HELEN_WARD_SUMMARY: Helen Ward is a member of the Old Guard and is responsible for logistics records.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_HOLLIS_SUMMARY: Information buyer. His real name is unknown. He maintains contacts within several factions and seems to know details of Directive Twelve before they become public. Different people may use the same name. He buys testimony, documents, routes, and details that can be verified before circulating within The Syndicate. His identity is deliberately uncertain, and some contacts suspect the name represents more than one person. He knows premature references to Directive Twelve and uses fragmented information to protect both his sources and his own position.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_HOWARD_FINCH_ROLE: Howard Finch is a member of KnoxNet.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_HOWARD_FINCH_SUMMARY: Howard Finch is a member of KnoxNet and is responsible for radio operation.

UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_ISAIAH_FREEMAN_ROLE: Isaiah Freeman is a member of New Knox Community.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_ISAIAH_FREEMAN_SUMMAR: Isaiah Freeman is a member of New Knox Community and is responsible for rural courier work.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_JESSE_CROWE_SUMMARY: Arms and supplies trafficker. He sells to almost anyone, although he observes personal limits that are difficult to interpret. At times he rejects profitable deals and accepts extremely dangerous ones without explaining why. He controls clandestine routes for weapons, ammunition, and restricted supplies for The Syndicate. He trades with almost any group able to pay but follows unexplained personal limits that can lead him to reject highly profitable deals. His inventory and contacts are useful, although every transaction helps arm players whose goals he rarely reveals.

UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_JUNE_WALKER_ROLE: Teacher and messenger for New Knox Community
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_JUNE_WALKER_SUMMARY: Former teacher and messenger. She travels between settlements carrying agreements, news, and requests for help. Her knowledge of families, routes, and local conflicts makes her indispensable. She uses her teaching experience to record names, needs, agreements, and news without depending entirely on radio. She travels dangerous roads between communities and knows which families can offer shelter, which routes are blocked, and which conflicts threaten each alliance. Her work holds New Knox Community together and makes her an especially valuable carrier of sensitive information.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_KEITH_MORGAN_ROLE: Keith Morgan is a member of the Old Guard.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_KEITH_MORGAN_SUMMARY: Keith Morgan is a member of the Old Guard and is responsible for patrol command.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_LAURA_KIM_ROLE: Laura Kim is a member of The Institute.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_LAURA_KIM_SUMMARY: Laura Kim is a member of The Institute and is responsible for clinical medicine.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_LENA_ORTIZ_ROLE: Old Guard rescue and evacuation sergeant
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_LENA_ORTIZ_SUMMARY: Security and evacuation specialist. She prioritizes rescues and openly questions orders she considers cruel or pointless. She oversees evacuation routes, rescues, perimeters, and security procedures for Old Guard. She favors solutions that reduce casualties and makes no effort to hide her disagreement when an order sacrifices people for prestige or territorial control. Her candor earns the trust of civilians and subordinates but creates constant tension with militarist elements.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_LEONARD_PRICE_ROLE: Leonard Price is a member of Knox Authority.
UI_KCMAIN_NPC_LORE_LEONARD_PRICE_SUMMARY: Leonard Price is a member of Knox Authority and is responsible for archives and courier work.
