UI_Lesson_LongBlunt_Beginner_P1: Baseball bats, crowbars, pipes, and two-handed clubs are among the most commonly found weapons in an urban environment. They require no edge maintenance and deliver devastating blunt force trauma.
UI_Lesson_LongBlunt_Beginner_P2: The principle is simple: concentrate force through a heavy striking surface. A baseball bat focuses the impact along its barrel. A crowbar adds the density of steel. The longer the weapon, the more momentum it generates — but the slower it swings.
UI_Lesson_LongBlunt_Beginner_P3: Grip with both hands spaced apart on the handle for control. The bottom hand anchors and directs, the top hand adds power. Keep your elbows slightly bent — locked elbows transmit shock painfully back into your joints on impact.
UI_Lesson_LongBlunt_Beginner_P4: Aim for the head. Blunt weapons against the body cause pain and broken bones but rarely incapacitate immediately. Against the undead, only cranial damage is effective. A solid two-handed swing to the skull is the most reliable stopping technique.

UI_Lesson_LongBlunt_Intermediate_P2: Hip rotation is the secret to powerful swings. The power chain runs from your legs through your hips into your arms. UI_Lesson_LongBlunt_Intermediate_P3: Against multiple zombies, use wide horizontal sweeps that can connect with several targets in one swing. UI_Lesson_LongBlunt_Intermediate_P4: Stamina management is critical with heavy weapons. Every full-power swing costs significant energy. UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Advanced_P1: Advanced maintenance goes beyond routine care into fabricating replacement parts, restoring neglected weapons, and improvising maintenance tools from common materials.
UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Advanced_P2: A sharpening kit can be improvised from natural materials. A flat river stone with fine grain works as a whetstone. The unglazed bottom ring of a ceramic mug makes an emergency blade hone. Car window glass fragments, while dangerous to handle, can strop an edge to razor sharpness.
UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Advanced_P3: Restoring a rusted weapon requires removing corrosion without damaging the base metal. Sand the rust with progressively finer abrasives — steel wool or sandpaper starting at 120 grit and finishing at 400. For deep pitting, accept cosmetic damage but ensure structural integrity before trusting the weapon in combat.
UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Advanced_P4: Spring fabrication from salvaged materials is possible for simple springs. Piano wire, baling wire, and clock springs can be shaped around a mandrel to approximate replacement springs. The spring rate won't match factory specs but may restore function to an otherwise useless weapon.

UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Beginner_P1: A well-maintained weapon lasts longer and performs reliably when your life depends on it. Neglected weapons break at the worst possible moment. Basic maintenance requires minimal tools and time.
UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Beginner_P2: After every use, clean your weapon. For bladed weapons, wipe the blade free of blood, dirt, and moisture with a dry cloth. For blunt weapons, check for cracks, dents, and loose components. For firearms, field-strip and remove carbon fouling from the barrel, bolt, and chamber.
UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Beginner_P3: Lubrication prevents rust and reduces friction on moving parts. A light coat of oil on metal surfaces protects against moisture. For firearms, apply oil sparingly to the slide rails, bolt carrier, and trigger mechanism. Over-oiling attracts dirt and can cause malfunctions — a thin film is all that's needed.
UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Beginner_P4: Storage matters. Keep weapons in a dry environment. Leather sheaths can trap moisture against a blade, causing rust. If storing long-term, apply a heavier coat of oil and wrap in an oiled cloth. Check stored weapons periodically for signs of corrosion.

UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Intermediate_P1: When replacement isn't an option, repair skills keep your weapons functional. Field repairs using available materials can extend a weapon's life significantly.
UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Intermediate_P2: Loose handles are the most common melee weapon failure. A loose axe head or bat that wiggles is dangerous. For wooden handles, soak the joint in water — wood swells and tightens. For a permanent fix, drive a wooden or metal wedge into the handle end inside the head. Wrap loose joints with wire or cord as a temporary measure.
UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Intermediate_P3: Bent blades can sometimes be straightened. Place the bent section over a flat surface and apply gradual pressure — never hammer directly on the edge. Repeated bending weakens metal, so a straightened blade should be considered compromised and replaced when possible.
UI_Lesson_Maintenance_Intermediate_P4: Firearm parts wear out in predictable order. Springs weaken first — magazine springs, recoil springs, and firing pin springs. Carry spares when available. Extractors chip from repeated use. A worn extractor causes failure-to-eject malfunctions. Learning which parts fail first lets you salvage from similar weapons proactively.

UI_Lesson_Masonry_Advanced_P1: Advanced masonry allows construction of arches, fireplaces, and reinforced structures that surpass basic wall construction in both strength and functionality.
UI_Lesson_Masonry_Advanced_P2: An arch spans an opening by transferring weight sideways into the walls on each side. Each wedge-shaped stone (voussoir) is held in place by the pressure of its neighbors. The center stone (keystone) locks the arch and must be placed last. Until the keystone is set, the arch needs temporary support (centering).
UI_Lesson_Masonry_Advanced_P3: Fireplace construction requires fire-resistant materials. The firebox lining should be firebrick (rated for high temperatures) set with refractory mortar. Regular brick and mortar will crack and crumble from repeated heating and cooling cycles.
UI_Lesson_Masonry_Advanced_P4: Reinforced masonry incorporates steel rebar within the wall. Rebar is placed vertically in the cores of hollow concrete blocks, which are then filled with concrete. This creates walls that resist lateral forces — critical for buildings in areas with high winds or seismic activity.

UI_Lesson_Masonry_Beginner_P1: Masonry creates the most permanent and fire-resistant structures possible. Stone and brick walls can stand for centuries and provide excellent protection from both weather and threats.
UI_Lesson_Masonry_Beginner_P2: Mortar is the binding agent that holds stones and bricks together. It is made by mixing cement, sand, and water into a thick paste. The ratio is typically one part cement to three parts sand, with water added gradually until the mixture holds its shape when squeezed but isn't too wet to work with.
UI_Lesson_Masonry_Beginner_P3: Laying bricks requires a level surface, consistent mortar thickness, and regular checking with a level and string line. Each course (row) should be level and the joints between bricks should be staggered — never stack joints directly above each other, as this creates a weak line that can crack the entire wall.
UI_Lesson_Masonry_Beginner_P4: Allow mortar to cure slowly for maximum strength. Rapid drying causes cracking and weak bonds. In hot weather, mist the wall with water periodically during the first 48 hours to slow the curing process.

UI_Lesson_Masonry_Intermediate_P1: Building load-bearing masonry walls requires understanding how forces travel through stone and brick. A poorly designed wall will crack and eventually collapse under its own weight.
UI_Lesson_Masonry_Intermediate_P2: Foundations are critical. A masonry wall must rest on a footing that spreads its weight over a wider area of ground. The footing should be below the frost line to prevent heaving in winter. Without a proper foundation, settling will crack the wall.
UI_Lesson_Masonry_Intermediate_P3: Thicker walls are stronger but use more material. A single-width brick wall (one brick thick) is suitable for interior partitions but not for exterior load-bearing walls. Double-width walls with the bricks interlocked provide much greater strength and insulation.
UI_Lesson_Masonry_Intermediate_P4: Openings for doors and windows weaken a wall because they interrupt the continuous brick pattern. A lintel — a strong horizontal beam of stone, concrete, or steel — must span each opening to support the weight above it. Without a lintel, the wall above the opening will sag and eventually collapse.

UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Advanced_P1: The transmission and drivetrain transfer engine power to the wheels. Understanding these systems lets you diagnose and repair problems that would otherwise leave a vehicle immobilized.
UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Advanced_P2: Manual transmissions use a clutch and gear set to match engine speed to wheel speed. The clutch connects and disconnects the engine from the gearbox. A worn clutch slips under load — the engine revs up but the vehicle doesn't accelerate proportionally. Clutch replacement is a major job requiring transmission removal.
UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Advanced_P3: Automatic transmissions use a torque converter and planetary gear sets to shift automatically. They require special transmission fluid that must be checked regularly. Low fluid causes slipping and overheating. Unlike manual transmissions, most automatic problems require specialized knowledge to repair.
UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Advanced_P4: The differential splits power between the drive wheels and allows them to turn at different speeds in corners. A whining or clunking noise from the rear of a rear-wheel-drive vehicle often indicates differential problems. The differential contains heavy gear oil that should be checked periodically.

UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Beginner_P1: Vehicles are invaluable for transportation, hauling supplies, and emergency escape. Understanding basic vehicle systems lets you perform simple repairs and keep a car running.
UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Beginner_P2: Every vehicle has five essential systems: engine, transmission, electrical, fuel, and braking. The engine converts fuel into mechanical power. The transmission transfers that power to the wheels. The electrical system starts the engine and powers lights and accessories. The fuel system stores and delivers gasoline. The brakes stop the vehicle safely.
UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Beginner_P3: Basic maintenance includes checking oil level, tire pressure, and coolant level. Low oil damages the engine permanently. Low tire pressure reduces fuel efficiency and causes uneven wear. Low coolant causes overheating, which can warp the engine block.
UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Beginner_P4: When salvaging vehicles, check the battery first — a dead battery is the most common reason a car won't start. Batteries can be charged from a running vehicle using jumper cables. Always connect positive to positive and negative to a ground point, never directly to the dead battery's negative terminal.

UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Intermediate_P1: Understanding engine internals lets you diagnose problems and perform repairs that keep vehicles operational long-term. Most engine issues stem from a few common failure points.
UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Intermediate_P2: Spark plugs ignite the fuel-air mixture in each cylinder. Fouled or worn spark plugs cause misfires, rough running, and poor fuel economy. They should be inspected regularly — a black sooty plug indicates a rich fuel mixture, while a white blistered plug indicates overheating.
UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Intermediate_P3: The alternator charges the battery while the engine runs. A failing alternator causes dim lights, slow cranking, and eventually a dead battery. A squealing belt often indicates the alternator belt is loose or worn. Check belt tension regularly and replace worn belts.
UI_Lesson_Mechanics_Intermediate_P4: Radiator hoses deteriorate over time, becoming soft, cracked, or swollen. A burst hose dumps all coolant quickly, causing rapid overheating. Carry spare hoses and clamps. In an emergency, duct tape can temporarily patch a small hose leak, but it won't last long under pressure and heat.

UI_Lesson_Pottery_Advanced_P1: Building a proper kiln gives you consistent, repeatable results and the ability to create more advanced ceramic pieces including pipes, tiles, and heat-resistant cookware.
UI_Lesson_Pottery_Advanced_P2: A simple updraft kiln can be built from firebrick or stacked stones with a firebox below and a chamber above. Hot air rises through the pottery chamber, heating the pieces evenly. A chimney at the top creates draft that feeds the fire. This design reaches much higher temperatures than a pit fire — essential for proper stoneware.
UI_Lesson_Pottery_Advanced_P3: Stoneware clay fires at higher temperatures than earthenware, producing extremely hard, dense ceramic that is naturally waterproof even without glaze. Stoneware is ideal for cookware because it can withstand direct flame without cracking.
UI_Lesson_Pottery_Advanced_P4: Ceramic pipes and tiles are valuable construction materials. Pipes can carry water or serve as drainage. Roof tiles provide fireproof roofing. Both require consistent thickness and careful drying to prevent warping. Use wooden forms or molds to ensure uniform shapes.

UI_Lesson_Pottery_Beginner_P1: Pottery creates watertight containers, cooking vessels, and storage jars from one of the most abundant natural materials: clay. With practice and a heat source, you can produce essential household items.
UI_Lesson_Pottery_Beginner_P2: Clay can be found near rivers, streams, and in areas where the soil is heavy and sticky when wet. Good pottery clay should be smooth, plastic (moldable), and free of large stones and organic material. Knead the clay thoroughly to remove air bubbles — trapped air causes pieces to explode during firing.
UI_Lesson_Pottery_Beginner_P3: The simplest forming technique is coil building: roll clay into long ropes and stack them in a spiral, smoothing the coils together as you build upward. This creates pots, bowls, and jars without any tools or equipment.
UI_Lesson_Pottery_Beginner_P4: Before firing, pottery must dry completely. This takes several days depending on thickness and humidity. Rushing the drying process causes cracking. Once dry, the piece is bisque-fired in a hot fire to harden it permanently.

UI_Lesson_Pottery_Intermediate_P2: A pit fire is the simplest kiln: dig a hole, place dried pottery inside surrounded by fuel (wood, dried dung, or charcoal), and burn for several hours. Temperature control is limited, but pit firing has been used for thousands of years. Build the fire slowly to avoid thermal shock that cracks the pieces.
UI_Lesson_Pottery_Intermediate_P3: Glazing makes pottery watertight and easier to clean. A glaze is a thin coating of minerals (often containing silica and flux) that melts into a glass-like surface during firing. Without glaze, uncoated pottery absorbs water and eventually breaks down.
UI_Lesson_Pottery_Intermediate_P4: For survival purposes, a simple salt glaze can be achieved by throwing handfuls of salt into the fire during peak temperature. The sodium vaporizes and bonds with the clay surface, creating a basic but functional waterproof coating.

UI_Lesson_Reloading_Advanced_P1: Advanced reloading extends beyond the weapon itself into ammunition selection, conservation, and the basics of reloading spent brass.
UI_Lesson_Reloading_Advanced_P2: Ammunition types matter. Full metal jacket rounds penetrate barriers but may pass through soft targets. Hollow points expand on impact, transferring more energy but penetrating less. Shotgun shells come in buckshot for large targets and birdshot for small game. Match your ammunition to the situation.
UI_Lesson_Reloading_Advanced_P3: Ammunition conservation is critical when resupply is uncertain. Every round should count. Prioritize aimed shots over suppressive fire. Keep a mental count of rounds remaining. Rotate older ammunition to the front of your supply — stored improperly, primers and powder degrade over years.
UI_Lesson_Reloading_Advanced_P4: Handloading allows you to reuse spent brass casings. A reloading press resizes the case, seats a new primer, measures powder, and presses in a fresh bullet. This requires precision — an overcharged round can destroy a weapon and injure the shooter. Use published load data and a quality powder scale. Never guess at powder charges.

UI_Lesson_Reloading_Beginner_P1: Reloading a firearm quickly and safely is as important as aiming it. A weapon with an empty magazine is dead weight. Understanding how ammunition feeds into your weapon lets you stay in the fight.
UI_Lesson_Reloading_Beginner_P2: Most modern firearms use detachable magazines. The magazine holds cartridges under spring pressure and feeds them into the chamber when the action cycles. To reload: release the empty magazine, insert a loaded one, and rack the slide or charging handle to chamber the first round.
UI_Lesson_Reloading_Beginner_P3: Revolvers load differently — cartridges sit in a rotating cylinder. Swing out the cylinder, eject spent cases with the ejector rod, insert fresh rounds, and close the cylinder. Speed loaders hold all rounds in the correct pattern and drop them in at once.
UI_Lesson_Reloading_Beginner_P4: Always keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction while reloading. Treat every weapon as if it is loaded, even during a reload. Never look down the barrel to check if the chamber is clear — use the ejection port or cylinder opening to visually inspect.

UI_Lesson_Reloading_Intermediate_P1: Under pressure, reload speed can save your life. Practiced technique turns a multi-second fumble into a smooth, automatic action.
UI_Lesson_Reloading_Intermediate_P2: The tactical reload swaps a partially empty magazine for a full one during a lull. Retain the partial magazine — it still has usable rounds. The emergency reload happens when the gun runs dry. Drop the empty magazine, slam a fresh one home, and release the slide stop in one fluid motion. Practice until it becomes muscle memory.
UI_Lesson_Reloading_Intermediate_P3: Malfunctions happen. The most common is a failure to feed — the round jams partway into the chamber. Clear it with tap-rack-bang: slap the magazine base to seat it, rack the slide sharply to eject the bad round and chamber a new one, then reassess and fire if needed.
UI_Lesson_Reloading_Intermediate_P4: A double feed — two rounds trying to enter the chamber — is more serious. Lock the slide back, rip out the magazine, rack the slide three times to clear both rounds, reinsert the magazine, and rack again to chamber. This takes practice under stress to perform reliably.

UI_Lesson_ShortBlade_Advanced_P1: Advanced short blade mastery involves understanding blade geometry, selecting the right tool for the job, and employing techniques that maximize a small weapon's effectiveness.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlade_Advanced_P2: Blade geometry determines function. A drop-point blade has a strong tip for piercing and a curved belly for slicing — the best all-around survival shape. A tanto point is extremely strong for piercing hard materials but poor for slicing. A clip-point offers a fine tip for precision work but is more fragile under heavy use.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlade_Advanced_P3: Fighting from a clinch — when grappled at close range — is where short blades truly shine. Hook the opponent's arm with your off hand and deliver short, repeated thrusts to accessible targets. Full slashing motions are impossible at this range. Economy of movement matters more than power.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlade_Advanced_P4: Dual-wielding a knife and a longer weapon covers both ranges. The primary weapon handles most encounters, while the knife activates only if the fight collapses to grappling distance. Transitioning between weapons requires practice — fumbling a transition under stress is worse than fighting with one weapon competently.

UI_Lesson_ShortBlade_Beginner_P1: Knives and short blades are the most personal of melee weapons. They excel in close quarters where larger weapons can't swing freely, and double as essential survival tools.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlade_Beginner_P2: The standard grip wraps all four fingers around the handle with the thumb on top. This provides maximum control for both cutting and thrusting. The reverse (icepick) grip holds the blade pointing downward from the fist — it generates powerful downward stabs but limits reach and versatility.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlade_Beginner_P3: A knife is primarily a thrusting weapon. Stabbing penetrates deeper than slashing and targets vital areas more precisely. Aim for soft tissue — the neck, inner thighs, and underarms are vulnerable. Against the undead, only the base of the skull or eye socket offers a reliable knife target.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlade_Beginner_P4: The biggest danger with a knife is closing to striking range. At knife distance you are within arm's reach of your opponent. Use a knife as a last resort when longer weapons aren't available, or as a backup when your primary weapon is lost or broken.

Keep the blade moving in small figure-eight patterns — a moving blade is harder to grab or predict than a stationary one.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlade_Intermediate_P3: The off hand serves as a shield and grapple tool. Keep it raised, palm out, to block or deflect incoming attacks. UI_Lesson_ShortBlunt_Advanced_P1: Advanced short blunt mastery means turning anything into a weapon and pairing a short blunt tool with complementary equipment.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlunt_Advanced_P2: Almost any dense, compact object becomes a short blunt weapon: a padlock in a sock (a makeshift flail), a heavy flashlight, a rock in your fist, a can of food, or a length of heavy chain. The key properties are: fits in one hand, dense enough to cause trauma, and won't shatter on impact.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlunt_Advanced_P3: Pairing a short blunt weapon with a shield dramatically increases survivability. A trash can lid, baking sheet, or car door panel blocks bites and grabs while your weapon hand delivers strikes. Lead with the shield to push into threats, then strike over or around it.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlunt_Advanced_P4: Reinforcing an improvised weapon improves its durability. Wrapping cloth around a glass bottle's neck prevents it from shattering on first impact. Duct-taping a heavy bolt to the end of a short pipe concentrates its mass. Every modification is a tradeoff between weight, speed, and durability.

UI_Lesson_ShortBlunt_Beginner_P2: The advantage of a short blunt weapon is speed. One-handed strikes are faster than two-handed swings, allowing rapid repeated blows. What they lack in single-hit power compared to long weapons, they make up for in versatility and availability.
UI_Lesson_ShortBlunt_Beginner_P3: A hammer is the ideal short blunt weapon. The concentrated head weight delivers maximum force to a small area. Claw hammers have the added benefit of a hooked back for piercing. Ball-peen hammers have a rounded striking face that prevents glancing blows.

UI_Lesson_Spear_Advanced_P1: Advanced spear work involves crafting purpose-built weapons with superior materials and learning to throw short spears as javelins.
UI_Lesson_Spear_Advanced_P2: A fire-hardened tip greatly improves a wooden spear. Char the sharpened tip in a fire until the outer layer carbonizes, then scrape off the char and resharpen. The heat drives out moisture and hardens the wood fibers. This treatment makes the tip significantly more durable against both bone and soft tissue.
UI_Lesson_Spear_Advanced_P3: Lashing a metal or stone point to the shaft creates a vastly superior weapon. Use a split-socket binding: split the shaft end, insert the point base into the split, and wrap tightly with cordage in an X pattern. Coat the binding with pine pitch or epoxy to waterproof and strengthen the joint.
UI_Lesson_Spear_Advanced_P4: Javelin throwing extends your kill range. A throwing spear should be lighter and shorter than a melee spear — about chest height and balanced slightly forward of center. Throw overhand with your body weight transferring forward. Practice at 10 to 15 meters first. The tradeoff: a thrown spear that misses leaves you unarmed.

UI_Lesson_Spear_Beginner_P1: The spear is humanity's oldest weapon and remains one of the most effective. It offers the greatest reach of any melee weapon, keeping threats at maximum distance while delivering lethal thrusts.
UI_Lesson_Spear_Beginner_P2: Hold the spear with your rear hand at the butt and your lead hand about one-third of the way from the tip. The rear hand provides power while the lead hand guides and aims. This two-point grip gives you both control and the ability to extend for maximum reach.
UI_Lesson_Spear_Beginner_P3: The thrust is the spear's primary attack. Extend your rear arm while guiding with the lead hand, driving the point straight into the target. Retract quickly to prevent the target from grabbing the shaft. A stuck spear is a lost spear.
UI_Lesson_Spear_Beginner_P4: A simple spear can be made from a sturdy pole sharpened to a point or fitted with a knife blade lashed to the end. Hardwood like oak or ash makes the best shaft — soft woods flex too much and snap under stress. The shaft should be about your height or slightly longer.

UI_Lesson_Spear_Intermediate_P2: Zone control means keeping the spear tip active in the space between you and threats. Small circular motions or quick feints discourage anything from closing in. If a zombie walks into your zone, thrust and reset. If it gets past the tip, you've lost the spear's advantage — transition to a shorter backup weapon or retreat.
UI_Lesson_Spear_Intermediate_P3: In group fighting, the spear excels in a line formation. Spear users stand shoulder to shoulder, presenting a wall of points that nothing can approach safely. UI_Lesson_Spear_Intermediate_P4: Sweeping strikes use the shaft to push back groups. A low horizontal sweep trips or staggers multiple targets. This isn't lethal but buys time to reset and deliver finishing thrusts to staggered enemies one at a time.

UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Advanced_P1: Advanced tailoring combines fabric skills with protective design. Padded and reinforced clothing can mean the difference between a scratch and a serious wound.
UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Advanced_P2: Padding absorbs impact by distributing force across a wider area. Multiple layers of fabric with cotton batting, foam, or even crumpled newspaper between them create effective padding. The thicker the padding, the more protection — but too much restricts movement. Focus padding on vital areas: torso, neck, and forearms.
UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Advanced_P3: Leather reinforcement on top of padding adds cut and bite resistance. Stitch leather panels over the padded garment at key points. Double-layer the leather at the forearms and shoulders where attacks are most likely to land.
UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Advanced_P4: Stitching quality determines how well armor holds together under stress. Use waxed thread for durability and reinforce all seams with double or triple rows of stitching. A seam that fails during a fight defeats the purpose of the armor entirely.

UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Beginner_P1: Clothing provides vital protection from weather, injury, and infection. Learning to mend torn clothing and sew basic garments extends the life of irreplaceable supplies.
UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Beginner_P2: The basic sewing kit contains needles, thread, scissors, and patches of fabric. A thimble protects your finger when pushing needles through tough material. Thread should match the weight of the fabric — heavy thread for denim, fine thread for lighter fabrics.
UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Beginner_P3: The running stitch is the simplest technique: push the needle in and out in a straight line. For stronger repairs, use a backstitch — after each forward stitch, go back half a stitch length before moving forward again. This creates an overlapping pattern that resists tearing much better than a simple running stitch.
UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Beginner_P4: Patching holes requires cutting a piece of fabric larger than the hole, placing it behind the damaged area, and stitching around all edges. For clothing that sees heavy use, reinforce stress points like knees, elbows, and seams with extra stitching before they fail.

UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Intermediate_P1: Building garments from raw fabric lets you replace clothing that's beyond repair and create specialized items like padded armor, rain gear, and insulated winter clothing.
UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Intermediate_P2: Patterns are the blueprint for garments. A pattern shows each piece that needs to be cut, including seam allowances — the extra fabric around each edge that gets folded and stitched. Without seam allowances, the finished garment will be too small.
UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Intermediate_P3: Denim, leather, and canvas are the most durable fabrics for survival clothing. Denim resists abrasion and tearing. Leather provides excellent protection from cuts and bites. Canvas is strong, water- resistant, and available from tarps, tents, and bags.
UI_Lesson_Tailoring_Intermediate_P4: Layering is more effective than a single thick garment. A base layer wicks moisture, a middle layer insulates, and an outer layer blocks wind and rain. Each layer can be added or removed as conditions change, giving you much better temperature control.

UI_Lesson_Tracking_Advanced_P1: Advanced tracking includes reading human sign for security purposes and understanding counter-tracking techniques to conceal your own movement.
UI_Lesson_Tracking_Advanced_P2: Human tracks reveal more than direction. Shoe tread patterns identify individuals — a distinctive wear pattern or sole type is as unique as a name. Load-bearing changes (deeper heels when carrying weight, asymmetric depth when carrying something on one side) indicate what the person was doing.
UI_Lesson_Tracking_Advanced_P3: Counter-tracking conceals your movement from others. Walk on hard surfaces when possible. Step on rocks, logs, and roots rather than soft ground. Walk through streams to break the trail. Brush out tracks in unavoidable soft areas with a branch — though a skilled tracker will notice brushed ground.
UI_Lesson_Tracking_Advanced_P4: Zombie tracking is simpler but vital. The undead drag their feet, creating scuff marks and drag lines rather than clean footprints. They travel in the direction of their last stimulus — noise or sight. A trail of zombie sign leading toward your base means you were detected. Multiple converging trails indicate a horde forming. Reading these patterns gives you advance warning to fortify or evacuate.

UI_Lesson_Tracking_Beginner_P1: Tracking is the art of reading the marks that people and animals leave on the landscape. In a survival situation, tracking locates game for food, detects approaching threats, and helps you navigate by following trails.
UI_Lesson_Tracking_Beginner_P2: A track is any impression left by a foot or hoof. Look for them in soft ground — mud, sand, snow, and damp soil hold prints best. Hard surfaces like asphalt and rock show scuff marks, displaced pebbles, and dirt transfers. Training your eye to spot these subtle signs takes practice.
UI_Lesson_Tracking_Beginner_P3: Track freshness tells you how recent the passage was. Fresh tracks have sharp edges and crisp detail. Over hours, edges crumble, rain washes detail away, and debris (leaves, dust) accumulates inside the print. In mud, a track fills with water from the sides over time — a dry track in wet ground is recent.
UI_Lesson_Tracking_Beginner_P4: Direction of travel is obvious from foot shape — the toe points forward. Stride length indicates speed: walking strides are short and even, running strides are long with deeper toe impressions. A dragging or uneven stride suggests injury.

UI_Lesson_Tracking_Intermediate_P1: Intermediate tracking identifies which animal made a set of tracks and follows a trail over difficult terrain where sign is sparse.
UI_Lesson_Tracking_Intermediate_P2: Animal tracks fall into recognizable families. Deer have two-toed heart-shaped hoofprints. Dogs and wolves show four toes with claw marks. Cats show four toes without claw marks (retracted claws). Rabbits leave distinctive paired prints — two large hind feet ahead of two small forefeet. Learning these basic shapes lets you identify game by track alone.
UI_Lesson_Tracking_Intermediate_P3: Beyond footprints, animals leave other sign: scat (droppings) reveals diet and species, rub marks on trees show territory boundaries, browse marks on plants indicate feeding areas, and bedding depressions show resting sites. Together, these signs paint a picture of animal behavior and patterns.
UI_Lesson_Tracking_Intermediate_P4: Following a trail over hard ground or through vegetation requires looking ahead, not down. Spot the next sign before leaving the last one. When you lose the trail, stop — don't walk forward destroying the last known sign. Instead, circle wide from the last confirmed track looking for the next one. This preserves the trail for a second attempt.

UI_Lesson_Trapping_Advanced_P1: Running an effective trap line is a systematic operation: setting multiple traps across a territory, checking them on a schedule, and processing the catch efficiently.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Advanced_P2: A trap line follows a circuit you can walk in a reasonable time. Space traps based on the target animal's territory size — closer together for small animals (rabbits: every 30 meters) and farther apart for larger ones. Mark each trap location discreetly so you can find them reliably.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Advanced_P3: Vary trap types along the line to target different species. Snares on trails for rabbits, deadfalls near dens for raccoons, and cage traps near water for muskrats. Diversity in your trap line produces a more consistent yield than targeting one species.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Advanced_P4: Process animals promptly after checking traps. Skin while the body is still warm — the hide separates from muscle more easily. Stretch and dry hides for later use in tailoring. The meat should be cooked, smoked, or dried the same day. Entrails make excellent bait for the next round of trapping.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Advanced_Q1_C3: Based on the target animal's territory size

UI_Lesson_Trapping_Beginner_P1: Trapping catches animals while you attend to other tasks. Unlike hunting, a trap line works for you around the clock, providing a passive source of protein and fur.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Beginner_P2: All traps work on the same principles: attract the animal with bait or place the trap in its path, then restrain or kill it with a mechanism triggered by the animal's movement. Understanding animal behavior — what they eat, where they travel, when they're active — is more important than the trap's complexity.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Beginner_P3: Cage traps capture animals alive in a wire or wooden enclosure. A trigger plate inside releases a door that falls shut when the animal steps on it. Cage traps are the safest to set and most humane, but they require frequent checking — trapped animals suffer in the elements.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Beginner_P4: Place traps along trails, near burrows, and beside water sources where animal sign (tracks, droppings, gnawed vegetation) indicates regular activity. A trap in the wrong location catches nothing no matter how well built.

UI_Lesson_Trapping_Intermediate_P1: Snares and deadfalls are the most field-expedient traps, built from natural materials found in any wooded environment.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Intermediate_P2: A simple snare is a loop of wire or cord set along an animal trail at head height for the target species. As the animal moves through, the loop tightens around its neck. Anchor the snare to something solid — a live tree or heavy stake. Use brass or steel wire for snares; cord is chewed through easily.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Intermediate_P3: Deadfall traps use a heavy weight (flat rock or log) propped up by a trigger mechanism. When the animal disturbs the trigger — usually by pulling bait — the weight falls. The figure-four trigger is the most common: three sticks notched to hold each other in tension, releasing when any piece is moved.
UI_Lesson_Trapping_Intermediate_P4: Scent control is critical. Human scent on a trap warns animals away. Handle traps with gloves, rub them with local vegetation, or boil them in water with bark and leaves. Place traps wearing boots you also wear while doing other outdoor work so your trail scent is already familiar to local wildlife.

UI_Lesson_Welding_Advanced_P1: Advanced metalworking involves fabricating custom parts: brackets, panels, containers, and structural reinforcements. Sheet metal work and precision fabrication open up possibilities that basic welding cannot achieve alone.
UI_Lesson_Welding_Advanced_P2: Sheet metal can be cut with tin snips, bent along straight lines using a brake or vise, and joined with rivets, screws, or spot welds. When bending sheet metal, score a line first with a sharp tool to ensure a clean, straight bend. Thin sheet bends easily but thick plate requires heat to prevent cracking.
UI_Lesson_Welding_Advanced_P3: Fabrication starts with a plan. Measure twice, cut once applies doubly to metal — mistakes waste scarce material and dull your tools. Make cardboard templates for complex shapes before cutting metal. Account for bend allowances — metal stretches at the bend point, so the finished piece will be slightly shorter than the flat pattern.
UI_Lesson_Welding_Advanced_P4: Heat treatment changes metal properties. Heating steel to red-hot and quenching in water hardens it, making it hold an edge but become brittle. Tempering (reheating to a lower temperature) reduces brittleness while retaining hardness. This is how tools and blades are made durable.

UI_Lesson_Welding_Advanced_Q4_C1: To make it as hard as possible

UI_Lesson_Welding_Beginner_P1: Metalworking allows you to create durable structures, repair vehicles, and build tools that wood alone cannot provide. Metal is stronger, more weather-resistant, and can be shaped when heated.
UI_Lesson_Welding_Beginner_P2: The essential tools for basic metalworking are a propane torch, a welding mask, and a metal saw or grinder. A propane torch provides enough heat to soften and join thin metal pieces. The welding mask protects your eyes from intense light and sparks.
UI_Lesson_Welding_Beginner_P3: Start by learning to cut metal cleanly. A hacksaw works for thin stock but is slow. An angle grinder with a cutting disc is faster but requires careful control — the disc can bind and kick back. Always wear eye protection and gloves when cutting metal.
UI_Lesson_Welding_Beginner_P4: Metal salvage is everywhere in an urban environment: sheet metal from signs, pipes from plumbing, angle iron from shelving, and steel from vehicles. Learn to identify different metals — steel is magnetic, aluminum is light, and copper has a distinctive color.

UI_Lesson_Welding_Intermediate_P1: Welding joins metal pieces by melting them together at the joint. It creates bonds stronger than the surrounding metal when done correctly. Several welding methods exist, but propane brazing and arc welding are the most practical for survival situations.
UI_Lesson_Welding_Intermediate_P2: Propane brazing uses a brass filler rod that melts at a lower temperature than the base metal. The filler flows into the joint by capillary action and solidifies into a strong bond. It works well for thin materials and copper pipe but isn't suitable for structural steel.
UI_Lesson_Welding_Intermediate_P3: Arc welding uses electricity to create an intense arc between an electrode and the workpiece. The heat melts both the electrode and the base metal, fusing them together. Arc welding creates the strongest joints and works on thick steel, but requires a generator or grid power to operate.
UI_Lesson_Welding_Intermediate_P4: Regardless of method, joint preparation is critical. Surfaces must be clean — rust, paint, and oil prevent proper bonding. Grind or wire brush the joint area until bare metal is exposed. A clean joint is the difference between a weld that holds and one that cracks.

UI_MNAM_Debug_tt:
Logs to console.txt what the mod decides about each room and building.
For bug reports: turn it on, reproduce the problem, and send the file.
Costs one line per event, nothing per frame.
UI_MNAM_Enable_tt:
Draws on your world map by itself as you search buildings.
Turn off and nothing new is ever drawn; marks already on the map stay.
UI_MNAM_HideServerWide: Hide marks shared with the whole server
UI_MNAM_HideServerWide_tt:
On a busy public server, the orange marks -- the ones somebody shared with EVERYONE -- become noise.
This hides only those. What your party and your safehouse shared stays visible.
Nothing is deleted. Turn it back off and they all return the next time you open the map.
The game has a blunter version of this in the map's own options, "Remote Symbols", which hides every mark from every other player at once.
UI_MNAM_IconPick_tt:
Which of the game's own map symbols this mark uses.
Change it any time: the next map you open redraws every mark of this kind with the new icon.
UI_MNAM_MarkComplete: Mark buildings with nothing left behind
UI_MNAM_MarkComplete_tt:
A building where no closed container is left in any room gets a checkmark instead of an X.
So the X means "been here" and the checkmark means "nothing left behind".
Rooms with no containers at all count as done. The swap happens the next time you open the map.
UI_MNAM_MarkScale_tt:
How big a mark is drawn, as a percentage of a symbol you place by hand.
The default is smaller than yours on purpose: in a dense neighbourhood -- a residential block, a row of townhouses -- full-size marks touch each other and the map stops being readable.
A building's mark sits on the building; the valuable-find mark is drawn SMALLER, hanging off its top-right corner, so the two never cover each other.
Changing this redraws every mark of the mod the next time you open the map.
UI_MNAM_MarkVehicles_tt:
Marks a car you inspected -- sat in, or opened the hood -- that still had fuel when you walked away.
A car merely seen from outside is never marked: you had no way to know.
UI_MNAM_MaxMarks_tt:
A ceiling on how many buildings this mod will ever draw.
The map recalculates the position of every symbol each time you zoom or drag, so thousands of them make the map sluggish.
Progress keeps being tracked past the ceiling; only the drawing stops.
UI_MNAM_MinRooms_tt:
How many rooms must count before the building gets an X.
One is too few: you can walk through a single room without searching anything.
Buildings with fewer rooms than this only need all of theirs, so sheds still get marked.
UI_MNAM_N3WODesc: These two options only do anything with the N3WO Map Overhaul mod installed. That mod knows the NAME of 949 buildings across Knox County; this one knows what you did inside them. Together the mark stops being an anonymous X.
UI_MNAM_N3WONotify: Say on screen what was marked
UI_MNAM_N3WONotify_tt:
A note across the top of the screen when a building is marked, or a valuable is left behind -- with the building's name when N3WO knows it.
This mod is otherwise invisible until you open the map: writing on the map needs the map screen open, and there is no way around that.
A name you have not discovered yet is never revealed: the mod does not tell you what you do not know.
UI_MNAM_N3WOOnlyPOI_tt:
Turns the mod inside out: instead of marking every house you searched, it marks only the places N3WO has a name for -- shops, stations, clinics.
In a long Louisville save this is the difference between a readable map and an X over every house.
Does nothing without N3WO installed: with no list of names, no building would ever be marked.
UI_MNAM_N3WOUsePins: Marks as N3WO points, not map symbols
UI_MNAM_N3WOUsePins_tt:
Puts every mark on N3WO's own point layer instead of drawing a map symbol.
You gain: the building's NAME on hover, a colour per kind of mark, the map's search box finding them, and one button to hide them all.
You lose: marks on the MINIMAP, marks when zoomed out past N3WO's threshold, and moving or erasing them with the map's own tools.
Turn it off and every mark goes back to being a symbol -- the swap happens the next time you open the map, in both directions, and nothing is left behind.
UI_MNAM_RareDesc: Marks a building where you SAW something valuable and left it. Only what you actually opened counts -- a generator in a cupboard you never opened is not marked, because you do not know it is there.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Axe_tt: Wood, doors, and a decent weapon in one item.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Blade_tt: The two melee weapons worth a trip back.
UI_MNAM_Rare_BlowTorch_tt:
The whole metalworking tree depends on it.
A spent one is never marked.
UI_MNAM_Rare_CarBattery_tt:
Turns an abandoned car into a working one.
A dead battery is never marked.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Crowbar_tt: The best durability-to-damage melee weapon in the game.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Firearm_tt: Shotgun, pistol, rifle -- any of them.
UI_MNAM_Rare_FishingRod_tt: Food that does not fight back.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Generator_tt:
The single most valuable find in the game.
Also marks generators already placed in the world.
UI_MNAM_Rare_HamRadio_tt: Long range information, and the only way to hear another survivor.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Medicine_tt: The things that save a character you were about to lose.
UI_MNAM_Rare_PropaneTank_tt:
Feeds the blowtorch, and makes bombs.
An empty tank is never marked.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Recipe_tt: Schematics and engineer magazines: they teach what XP does not.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Saw_tt: A prerequisite for most of carpentry.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Seeds_tt: Only matters if you farm -- turn it off if you do not.
UI_MNAM_Rare_SewingKit_tt: Clothing repair, and the padding that stops bites.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Sledgehammer_tt: Demolition. Without one, half the map's walls are permanent.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Tarp_tt: Tents, rain collectors, and covered storage.
UI_MNAM_Rare_Welding_tt: Mask and rods -- the pair the blowtorch needs.
UI_MNAM_RequireWritingTool_tt:
You can only draw on a map with something to write with, so neither can this mod.
Progress is still tracked without one: find a pencil and the missing marks appear the next time you open the map.
UI_MNAM_RoomSeconds_tt:
How long you must spend in a room for it to count as searched -- unless you open a container there, which counts it instantly.
Together these stop a building from being marked because you ran through it fleeing a horde: nobody opens cupboards while running away.
Real seconds, not in-game ones. Time spent sprinting never counts.
UI_MNAM_ShareDesc: Put a mark on the map for your group, and tell at a glance who can see it. On the map screen, bottom left, the "Share" button picks who; then take an icon from the normal palette and click. The mark comes out already coloured and synced -- PINK for your party, TEAL for your safehouse, ORANGE for the whole server. The game's own five pen colours stay private, yours only. Server only: in single player the button is not there.
UI_MNAM_Share_NoFaction: you are not in a party
UI_MNAM_Share_Tooltip: Who sees the next mark you place. Click to change.
UI_MNAM_SkipSafehouse_tt: Your own base is not loot, and an X over it is noise.
UI_MNAM_VehicleFuelMin_tt: Below this, the tank is not worth a trip back with a gas can.

UI_MSM_Dialog_FullSaveBody2: What would you like to do after saving?
UI_MSM_EditMods_AfterBody: The new save will list only kept mods. Items, recipes, or vehicles from removed mods may appear as broken on first load.
UI_MSM_EditMods_HowBody: Edit Mods always operates on a clone of the save. Your original is never touched.
UI_MSM_EditMods_MaintenanceBody: Edit Mods is temporarily disabled while I'm reworking the duplicate-with-removed-mods flow. The button will return in a future patch. All other operations (Load, Save, Duplicate, Rename, Delete) are unaffected.

UI_MSM_EditMods_Subtitle: %1 mods in save · %2 missing · %3 dependencies · %4 selected to remove
UI_MSM_Help_AIPlaceholders_02: The "Default image" thumbnail style ships AI-generated placeholder art so saves without a screenshot are not blank.
UI_MSM_Help_AIPlaceholders_03: These images are filler. They are intentionally generic and meant to be replaced over time.
UI_MSM_Help_AIPlaceholders_05: If you are an artist and would like your work to replace these placeholders in a future release, get in touch via the Workshop comments. You will be credited.
UI_MSM_Help_AIPlaceholders_06: Submissions should be 16:9 landscape JPG or PNG, at least 1280x720 (1920x1080 preferred), matching the format of the existing placeholders.
UI_MSM_Help_BackupDir_02:
The backup folder is where Manual Save stores your save slots.
Each slot is a subfolder organised by game mode and world name.
UI_MSM_Help_BackupDir_04: If left empty, slots are stored in:
UI_MSM_Help_BackupDir_07:
Type a full path and press Enter or click away to save.
The folder must already exist on disk.
UI_MSM_Help_BackupDir_09:
The Watcher reads this setting once at startup.
Restart it after changing the path.
UI_MSM_Help_BackupDir_10: Until then, saves continue going to the old location.
UI_MSM_Help_BackupDir_12:
Click Reset to default to return to the default location.
Existing saves in the old folder are not moved automatically.
UI_MSM_Help_CrashBackup_02: If the game crashes or is killed while a save was in progress, the Watcher detects the abandoned session and turns it into a recovery backup.
UI_MSM_Help_CrashBackup_03: Crashes are detected automatically. You don't need to do anything to enable this.
UI_MSM_Help_CrashBackup_05: When the game starts cleanly, the Watcher checks for sessions that never closed. Any orphaned save folder is copied to a new slot named with a _crash_<timestamp> suffix.
UI_MSM_Help_CrashBackup_06: Your original save is never deleted by this process.
UI_MSM_Help_CrashBackup_08: On the next main menu after a crash, a popup lists the recovered slots so you can find them in the Load screen.
UI_MSM_Help_CrashBackup_10: Treat them like any other manual save. Load to inspect, rename to keep, delete once you've confirmed everything is fine.
UI_MSM_Help_CrashBackup_11: They may contain partial world state if the crash happened mid-save. Don't blindly overwrite a good slot with one without checking.
UI_MSM_Help_CrashBackup_13:
Clean shutdowns (Exit to menu, Save & Exit, Save & Return) never produce _crash_ backups.
This is only for unexpected terminations.
UI_MSM_Help_Delete_02: Permanently removes the slot folder and thumbnail.
UI_MSM_Help_Delete_03:
There is no recycle bin.
Once confirmed, the data is gone.
UI_MSM_Help_Delete_05:
A dialog asks before deleting.
You must explicitly confirm to proceed.
UI_MSM_Help_Delete_07:
Only the selected slot is removed.
Other slots in the same world stay intact.
If a temporary vanilla copy was created by a Load, it is also removed.
Exported copies (slot_exported) are never touched.
UI_MSM_Help_Duplicate_02:
Creates an independent full-folder copy of the
selected save. The original is untouched.
UI_MSM_Help_Duplicate_04:
First copy:  MySlot_copy
If taken:    MySlot_copy_(2)
Then:        MySlot_copy_(3) and so on.
UI_MSM_Help_Duplicate_05:
The dialog pre-fills the next free name.
Type any name you prefer before confirming.
UI_MSM_Help_Duplicate_07:
A duplicate is a full folder copy.
200 MB save = +200 MB on disk. Use deliberately.
UI_MSM_Help_Duplicate_09:
Duplicate before risky moves (NPC raids, events).
Duplicate then Edit Mods: create a minimal mod snapshot
you can boot if a future PZ patch breaks a mod.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_02:
Edit Mods shows every installed mod alongside the ones recorded in the save.
Mods in the save start checked. Checked = included in the clone.
Uncheck a mod to drop it; check an unchecked mod to add it.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_03: The original slot is always kept. Edit Mods only creates clones.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_06: Mod is in the save and installed. Starts checked. Safe to keep or uncheck.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_08:
Mod is installed but not in this save. Starts unchecked.
Check it to add it to the clone's mod list.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_10:
Mod is listed in the save but not installed on this PC. Starts checked.
Use Exclude missing to uncheck all amber mods at once.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_12:
Exclude missing  - unchecks all amber mods at once.
Reset            - restores all checkboxes to the original save state.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_14: Uncheck mods to remove them from the clone, or check unchecked mods to add them.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_15: Use Sort and the category dropdown to browse. Search filters by name.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_16: Give the clone a name at the bottom and click Create copy.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_18:
The clone lists only the checked mods in its mods.txt.
Mod content already in the world (items, structures) is not changed.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_19: The original slot stays untouched. Load it to return to the full mod state.
UI_MSM_Help_EditMods_20: Items, recipes, vehicles, or traits from removed mods will appear broken on first load of the clone.
UI_MSM_Help_ExportVanilla_02:
Creates a standalone copy of a manual save slot in PZ's standard
save folder, visible in the vanilla load screen without this mod.
UI_MSM_Help_ExportVanilla_04:
The copy is named SLOT_exported in PZ's save folder.
This keeps it separate from the temporary copy created by Load.
UI_MSM_Help_ExportVanilla_06:
Deleting the original slot does NOT remove the exported copy.
The exported copy is yours to manage from the vanilla load screen.
UI_MSM_Help_ExportVanilla_08:
The thumbnail is cropped to 250x250 from the center of the
original screenshot, matching PZ's native thumbnail size.
UI_MSM_Help_ExportVanilla_10:
Sharing a save with someone who does not have the mod.
Keeping a vanilla copy as a permanent checkpoint.
Migrating away from the mod entirely.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_02:
A save that exits to the main menu, lets PZ flush
all in-memory state to disk, then copies the
consistent folder to a backup slot.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_03:
The only save type guaranteed to capture
the full world state.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_06:
Saves, returns to the main menu, stays there.
Use when you actually want to stop playing.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_07:
1. A screenshot is taken before the game closes.
2. The game exits to the main menu.
   This lets PZ write all data to disk completely.
3. The Watcher copies the save folder to a backup slot.
4. The main menu appears. The save is done.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_09:
Saves, returns to menu briefly, then immediately
reloads the world. Reliable as Full Save.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_10:
1. A screenshot is taken before the game closes.
2. The game exits to the main menu.
3. The Watcher copies the save folder to a backup slot.
4. The game automatically reloads the slot you just saved.
   No button press needed.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_12: Save & Return calls quit() then re-enters the world.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_13:
In exclusive fullscreen the GPU display mode swaps
twice - some drivers leave the screen blank/stuck.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_14:
Options > Display > Borderless Windowed.
The compositor handles the round-trip cleanly.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_16:
Everything: player, inventory, world, every chunk,
all zombies, weather, in-game clock.
Thumbnail is captured before the quit.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_18:
Default to Full Save - it is the only trustworthy
backup. Cost: time to exit and re-enter the world.
UI_MSM_Help_Fullsave_19:
End of session, the before-bed save.
Before any mod change.
Before Edit Mods or Rename World operations.
Any time there is no specific reason for Quick Save.
UI_MSM_Help_General_02: Takes a screenshot at the moment of each save and uses it as the slot thumbnail in the load screen.
UI_MSM_Help_General_03: If disabled, slots show a placeholder image instead.
UI_MSM_Help_General_05: Shows a confirmation dialog before loading a save.
UI_MSM_Help_General_06: Disable it if you find the extra click unnecessary.
UI_MSM_Help_General_08: Shows a confirmation dialog before permanently deleting a slot.
UI_MSM_Help_General_09: Leave this on. Deleted slots cannot be recovered from the load screen.
UI_MSM_Help_General_11:
Shows a warning strip at the bottom of the screen when the Watcher is not running.
Saves and screenshots require the Watcher.
UI_MSM_Help_General_12: Disable it if you run the Watcher manually and find the reminder distracting.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_02:
Named manual backup. Folder at
ManualSaves/<gmode>/<world>/<slot>/.
Multiple slots can belong to the same world.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_04:
A PZ world folder (Sandbox/Riverside, etc.).
Contains chunks, zombie data, weather, seed.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_06:
PZ game mode group: Sandbox, Apocalypse,
Survivor, Builder, Custom.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_08:
The external Windows process (Watcher.cmd/.ps1) that
performs file operations Lua cannot.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_10:
Small .txt files in Zomboid/Lua/ used to pass
commands and results between Lua and Watcher.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_12:
A counter the Watcher increments every tick.
If it stops changing, the game knows Watcher died.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_14:
Instant in-game backup. Fast but state held only
in memory (zombies, weather) may not match.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_16:
Backup that exits to main menu so PZ flushes
everything before the copy. Slower, fully consistent.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_18:
Full Save that auto-reloads the slot it just saved.
Works best in Borderless Windowed display mode.
UI_MSM_Help_Glossary_20:
Creates a clone of a slot with a custom mod list.
Checked mods are included; unchecked are excluded.

UI_MSM_Help_Safety_02:
Yes. The mod ships open .ps1 and .cmd scripts,
both plain text, both readable in Notepad.
UI_MSM_Help_Safety_03:
Nothing in the mod has network access.
Nothing modifies the PZ executable.
Uninstall returns your saves to vanilla state.
UI_MSM_Help_Safety_05:
On a 500ms loop it does four things:
1. Reads small .txt signal files from Zomboid/Lua/.
2. Copies, moves, or deletes folders in Zomboid/
   using robocopy.
3. Runs PowerShell to capture the game window.
4. Writes a Done file back so the game sees the result.
UI_MSM_Help_Safety_06:
No registry edits.
No external network calls.
No background services or autostart.
UI_MSM_Help_Safety_08:

Task Manager > Details: Watcher = powershell.exe
UI_MSM_Help_Safety_09: with ManualSave_Watcher.ps1 in the command line.
UI_MSM_Help_Safety_10: Resource Monitor > Network: no sockets opened.
UI_MSM_Help_Safety_12:
Some AVs flag any unsigned .ps1 that calls
robocopy - a heuristic, not a real
detection of malicious behaviour.
UI_MSM_Help_Safety_13:
Read the file first, then decide.
If you don't trust it: don't run it.
Lua side stays disabled; PZ behaves as vanilla.
UI_MSM_Help_Safety_14:
Both files are byte-identical across all Steam
Workshop installs of the same mod version.

UI_Manual_Chapter1_Text:
Pin tumbler mechanism is commonly used and most available mechanism for padlocks and cylinder door locks.
Main elements of pin tumbler lock mechanisms for us are driver pins, key pins and lock cylinder.
Driver pins drive key pins into the holes of the lock cylinder. Key pins are the parts that interact with any key.
When all driver pins align on the outer edge of the lock cylinder. Lock cylinder becomes unbound.
With a rotational force (for example by sturdy bent hairpin) an unbound lock opens without opposition.
Same things happen with the correct key. By putting the key in, driver pins align at the edge of the lock cylinder and the lock gets unbound.
By turning it, it unlocks. With a wrong key driver pins won't get aligned, the lock doesn't get unbind and turning the key won't be possible.
UI_Manual_Chapter1_Title: How Does Pin Tumbler Locks Work
UI_Manual_Chapter2_Text:
While a key, both align pins and apply rotational force. Lockpicking separates rotational force and pin alignment goals into different tools.
Rotation force is handled by the tension bar and pin alignment handled by the picker.
These two tools must be used together to compensate for the fact that they can't align all the pins at the same time as a key does.
Since it is hard to see small changes in tension we will use this tension meter to visualize the amount of tension applied.
When the rotational force is applied to a lock with a tension bar, pins get stuck by a particular order called binding order. The order is determined by imperfections of the lock mechanism.
Binding pin is the one that you should set other pins. This also fits the binding order as it should be.
When too much tension is applied, current binding pin will be the first one to get stuck. Stuck pins don't move.
Once enough tension is applied and the pin is lifted by picker to correct position. Pin gets set with a click sound. After this next pin in binding order, will be binding pin.
As pins get set, tension needs to be raised for the next binding pin to respond.
If tension gets too low, set pins and stuck pins will start to fall according to binding order with a click.
When all pins set the lock becomes unbound and it can be opened by further rotating the tension bar (increasing tension).
Every lock has its own binding order and it wouldn't change the second time you pick the same lock.
UI_Manual_Chapter3_Text:
Purpose of the game is opening the lock by finding the right tension range for each pin and setting them according to binding order.
Use the A and D keys to adjust tension. With a low lockpicking skill, your hands will tremble, which can subsequently lead to excessive tension. Too much tension can break your tools!
Move the mouse to lift each pin. Listen for a click when it sets correctly.
When all pins are set, you can open the lock by increasing the tension to the end.
UI_Manual_Chapter4_Text:
Security pins are made to make locks harder to manipulate with other tools than its key.
When used, security pins replace driver pins.
Mushroom pins are usually replace by first and last driver pin to make lock harder to pick.
What is special about mushroom pin is, when too much tension is used to set the pin, pin makes a false set with a click sound.
To avoid false set you need to keep tension bellow a certain amount. While this amount is always the same, it's place changes according to pin.
Another way to overcome this is keeping mushroom pin above its neck.

UI_NECROA_TT_AB: Anabolic Boost - Virus manipulates the pituitary gland (responsible for controlling other organs in the endocrine system) to generate more testosterone to aid in muscle buildup, resulting in zombies becoming extremely muscular and heavier.
UI_NECROA_TT_AE: Acute Encephalitis - Virus begins to cause multiple sources of swelling within the brain, resulting in severe neurological damage often resulting in death.
UI_NECROA_TT_AP: Ambush Predation - Reanimated zombies change behaviour and stay still, allowing zombies to ambush their prey if they get too close.
UI_NECROA_TT_AR: Acidic Reflux - Virus causes extreme laryngopharyngeal reflux, causing saliva to become acidic.
UI_NECROA_TT_AS: Adrenal Surge - Virus manipulates the adrenal cortex (the glands on top of your kidneys), causing it to mutate and produce an excess of adrenaline, resulting in zombies becoming more alert and aware of their surroundings.
UI_NECROA_TT_Air_Icon: Air 1 - Virus is capable of bypassing the alveolar macrophages (your lungs' filters), resulting in infection of the lungs. (Being around a body for roughly 10-15 minutes guarantees infection)
UI_NECROA_TT_Air_Icon2: Air 2 - Virus gains the ability to travel on air particles and dust (being around bodies for 7 minutes causes infection).
UI_NECROA_TT_Air_Icon3: Air 3 - Virus is capable of rapid replication in oxygen-exposed organs and injuries. (Being around bodies for 3-5 minutes causes infection)
UI_NECROA_TT_Anaerobic_Resuscitation_Ico: Anaerobic Resuscitation - Brain cells infected with the virus begin switching to anaerobic respiration, resulting in a buildup of lactic acid that destroys higher brain functions including personality and higher brain processing. Memory appears to be intact. (Zombies begin losing their ability to form proper sentences or words)
UI_NECROA_TT_Autophagia: Autophagia - Virus manipulates the brain's signals further to encourage biting or even consumption of one's own body.
UI_NECROA_TT_Autothysis: Autothysis - Virus begins weaponising the decomposition of the zombies to release methane and hydrogen sulphide, resulting in zombies exploding upon contact with fire. (Zombies explode when shot with guns or cremated; recommended to use arrows)
UI_NECROA_TT_BD: Bone Dysplasia - Bones accelerated by the excess of HGH begin to become denser, resulting in zombies becoming more resilient to trauma. (Zombies become very difficult to kill via melee weapons or small-calibre guns)
UI_NECROA_TT_Bat_Icon: Bats 1 - Bats become susceptible to infection. (Eating bats has a 50%% chance to infect you)
UI_NECROA_TT_Bat_Iconblack: Bats 2 - Virus begins to manipulate the brain of bats to encourage aggression and swarming (often resulting in large bat attacks that cause infections and deaths).
UI_NECROA_TT_Bird_Icon: Birds 1 - Avian species become susceptible to the virus (birds have a 60%% risk of being infected).
UI_NECROA_TT_Bird_Iconblack: Birds 2 - Virus begins to manipulate the brain of avian species, encouraging them to attack humans in order to spread the virus. (Birds are guaranteed to have the infection and become aggressive)
UI_NECROA_TT_Blood_Icon: Blood 1 - Virus is capable of entering the heart via veins.
UI_NECROA_TT_Blood_Icon2: Blood 2 - Virus is capable of replicating in the bloodstream.
UI_NECROA_TT_CE: Cranial Elephantitis - Virus manipulates the pituitary gland and adenoma to create a mutated version of human growth hormone (HGH), resulting in bones (especially around the skull) growing even to the point of deformation. (Zombies become more resistant to headshots)
UI_NECROA_TT_CM: Cranial Metastasis - Virus causes neurological development within the lungs, allowing decapitated zombies to still function and reanimate.
UI_NECROA_TT_CR1: Cold Resistance 1 - Virus becomes resilient to colder temperatures, allowing it to survive better in colder climates or environments.
UI_NECROA_TT_CR2: Cold Resistance 2 - Virus begins to lower its intracellular water level, making it harder for the virus to freeze and die, allowing it to survive in extremely cold environments or climates.
UI_NECROA_TT_CS: Cathemeral Shift - Virus causes more stimulation within the visual cortex (the part of the brain that processes what we see), causing the eyes to see better in sunlight.
UI_NECROA_TT_Cannibalism: Cannibalism - Virus causes an extreme compulsion to consume other members of its own species.
UI_NECROA_TT_Coma: Coma - Virus causes a buildup of pressure in the brain stem, resulting in loss of consciousness and occasional death.
UI_NECROA_TT_Cytopathic_Reanimation_Icon: Cytopathic Reanimation - Virus begins re-activating within the dead cells of a host and forms complex neural structures that reanimate the cells of the host, effectively turning the dead into zombies.
UI_NECROA_TT_DC: Dermal Calcification - The endocrine system (the organs responsible for hormones) becomes mutated by the virus, resulting in other parts of the body hardening and calcifying. (Zombies are even harder to kill via melee or ranged weapons)
UI_NECROA_TT_DF: Drifting Fermentation - Virus begins to control the decomposition process, causing zombies to bloat and be capable of drifting in sea currents.
UI_NECROA_TT_DM: Dyskinetic Movement - Zombies within the horde begin to have involuntary movements to increase co-ordination of the horde itself.
UI_NECROA_TT_DR: Autolytic Delay - Virus begins releasing its own digestive enzymes from the lysosomes (responsible for garbage disposal in the cell) present in the body, slowing the decay of the body.
UI_NECROA_TT_DR1: Drug Resistance 1 - Virus becomes resistant to Class 1 and Class 2 antivirals.
UI_NECROA_TT_DR2: Drug Resistance 2 - Virus becomes resistant to Class 3 and Class 4 antivirals.
UI_NECROA_TT_ED: Epidermal Digestion - Virus begins releasing digestive cells that salvage nutrients from the skin to re-activate cells, allowing corpses that are severely mutilated to re-animate.
UI_NECROA_TT_EMC: Enhanced Motor Control - Nutrient flow to the parietal lobe (responsible for processing touch, position and spatial awareness) increases, causing movement and co-ordination to improve. (Zombies become better at moving and become fast shamblers)
UI_NECROA_TT_EQ: Engorged Quadriceps - Zombies begin using nutrients from themselves or from feeding on other corpses to keep leg muscles repaired, allowing the horde to move faster.
UI_NECROA_TT_ES: Enhanced Sensory Integration - Nutrient flow to the occipital and temporal lobes (sight and sound processing) increases, resulting in stronger hearing and sight.
UI_NECROA_TT_Echopraxia: Echopraxia - Due to damage within the frontal lobe caused by the virus, zombies begin mimicking the movement patterns of zombies around them, allowing hordes to navigate around obstacles better.
UI_NECROA_TT_Fever: Fever - Virus begins to trigger fevers in the body, resulting in loss of concentration.
UI_NECROA_TT_GH: Genetic Hardening - Virus becomes harder to analyse under microscopes, making development of a cure slower.
UI_NECROA_TT_GR1: Genetic Reshuffle 1 - Virus begins to change its DNA strands, requiring more work needed to make a cure.
UI_NECROA_TT_GR2: Genetic Reshuffle 2 - Virus creates another strain of itself, requiring even more work for a cure to be created.
UI_NECROA_TT_Gastroenteritis: Gastroenteritis - Virus causes the gastrointestinal tract (GI) to become inflamed, causing frequent vomiting.
UI_NECROA_TT_Genome_Icon: Segmented Genome - Virus is capable of splitting into smaller molecules (increases chances of new evolutions per day).
UI_NECROA_TT_HI: Horde Instinct - Zombies gain an instinct to group up and begin travelling to search for prey.
UI_NECROA_TT_HI1: Horde Mentality - Lone zombies become more likely to follow hordes for food.
UI_NECROA_TT_HP: Horde Pheromones - Leaders within the horde will produce pheromones that attract zombies to it.
UI_NECROA_TT_HR1: Heat Resistance 1 - Virus becomes more resilient to heat and is more capable of surviving hotter environments or climates.
UI_NECROA_TT_HR2: Heat Resistance 2 - Virus avoids cellular breakdown in high temperatures, allowing it to survive in extremely hot climates and environments.
UI_NECROA_TT_HS: Hyper Salivation - Virus causes inflammation of the submandibular glands (responsible for a majority of saliva production), resulting in uncontrollable saliva production.
UI_NECROA_TT_HV: Horde Vocalisation - Leaders within the horde will make distinctive moans to attract more zombies to the horde.
UI_NECROA_TT_Hyperosmia: Hyperosmia - Virus causes the nasal epithelium (cellular lining of your nasal cavity) to become thinner, causing zombies to have an enhanced sense of smell.
UI_NECROA_TT_Insect_Icon: Insect - Insects (such as mosquitoes and flies) become carriers of the virus.
UI_NECROA_TT_Insomnia: Insomnia - Virus causes irritation of the eyes, resulting in the inability to sleep comfortably.
UI_NECROA_TT_LH: Lumbrical Hypertrophy - Virus causes the grip of a host to become stronger via manipulation of muscles and joints in the arm and hand.
UI_NECROA_TT_LN: Liquefactive Necrosis - Reanimated zombies begin to have their organs liquify and become easier to rupture, allowing them to survive without them and potentially cause further infection.
UI_NECROA_TT_LR: Liquefactive Resistance - Virus denatures (changes the natural qualities and structure of) hydrolytic enzymes (responsible for breaking larger molecules into smaller ones), delaying liquefactive necrosis and slowing decay even more.
UI_NECROA_TT_MT: Masticatory Tension - Virus begins strengthening the masticatory muscles (muscles around the jaw), resulting in the infected being able to bite through thick clothing like jumpers and jackets. (Zombies can cause more damage to clothing and have more of a chance to bite through thicker clothes)
UI_NECROA_TT_Mummification: Mummification - Zombies will begin entering a state of hibernation and mummification when in a very late stage of decay.
UI_NECROA_TT_NM: Naja Mortis - Virus increases muscle growth around the submandibular duct (the main path for saliva to get under your tongue), allowing zombies to projectile spit their acidic saliva at prey.
UI_NECROA_TT_Nausea_Icon: Gastrointestinal Expansion - Virus is capable of replication in stomachs and intestines; fecal matter and vomit can become sources of infection.
UI_NECROA_TT_PR: Putrefactive Resistance - Virus begins attacking anaerobic microorganisms that digest proteins from the body, causing decay to slow even more.
UI_NECROA_TT_PS: Peptide Surge - Virus manipulates the hormones in the brain to accelerate metabolism of fat to build muscle, resulting in zombies becoming physically stronger.
UI_NECROA_TT_Paranoia: Delirium - Virus begins reducing rational thought processing, resulting in an overwhelming sense of paranoia and irrational thinking.
UI_NECROA_TT_PhotophobiaIcon: Photophobia - Eyes become extremely sensitive to sunlight, resulting in irritation and pain.
UI_NECROA_TT_Polyphagia: Polyphagia - Virus begins manipulating the brain's hunger signals, resulting in compulsive hunger to consume meat more.
UI_NECROA_TT_Psychosis: Psychosis - Virus begins manipulating emotions, resulting in psychotic episodes and bursts of extreme violence toward themselves or others.
UI_NECROA_TT_RA: Regenerative Activation - Virus becomes capable of re-activating cells within a dead zombie's brain, causing the zombie to reanimate again.
UI_NECROA_TT_RB: Regenerative Bio-Synthesis - Virus enhances neurological regeneration, allowing zombies with severe head wounds to re-animate again.
UI_NECROA_TT_Rodent_Icon: Rats 1 - Fleas become susceptible to the infection and begin to use rats to spread it (rats become impossible to eat without infection).
UI_NECROA_TT_Rodent_Iconblack: Rats 2 - Rats become susceptible to the virus; the virus also triggers aggression in the brain, resulting in rats biting humans more often (rats become hostile).
UI_NECROA_TT_ST: Structured Travel - Zombies begin focusing on the horde leaders rather than themselves more.
UI_NECROA_TT_Saliva_Icon: Saliva 1 - Virus is capable of rapidly replicating in the salivary glands (bites from zombies have a 50/50 chance to infect).
UI_NECROA_TT_Saliva_Icon2: Saliva 2 - Virus is capable of rapidly replicating in nasal cavities (bites from zombies have a 90%% chance of infecting).
UI_NECROA_TT_TL: Temporal Lobe Manipulation - Virus manipulates the brain's temporal lobe to change behaviour regarding consumption of corpses, resulting in zombies ignoring corpses and instead focusing on movement. (Zombies ignore dead corpses if a player is seen)
UI_NECROA_TT_Urogenital_Icon: Urogenital Expansion - Virus is capable of replication in kidneys and urinary tracts. Other fluids are also capable of being contaminated (except for blood).
UI_NECROA_TT_VH: Vampiric Hunger - Virus manipulates hunger signals further to encourage the zombie to drink the blood of their prey instead of eating the flesh, leaving their prey more intact and easier to infect.
UI_NECROA_TT_Water_Icon: Water 1 - Virus is capable of living outside a living body in fresh warm water (water from rivers and lakes becomes unsafe to drink unless it has been treated/filtered).
UI_NECROA_TT_Water_Icon2: Water 2 - Virus is capable of surviving in chemically treated water (filtering water no longer works; rain water will have to become your primary source of water from now on).
UI_NECROA_TT_Zoonotic_Icon: Zoonotic Shift - Virus gains the ability to infect animals and allows cross-species infection (animals can infect animals that can then infect humans).
UI_NECROA_Welcome_L03: This mod is more than just zombies.
UI_NECROA_Welcome_L05: Wear a mask and gloves whenever possible.
UI_NECROA_Welcome_L07: Blood can infect you if you have open cuts.
UI_NECROA_Welcome_L08: Bandages will count as an open cut.
UI_NECROA_Welcome_L10: Do not drink directly from sinks.
UI_NECROA_Welcome_L11: Water is tainted and becomes dangerous
UI_NECROA_Welcome_L15: limited protection and raise your risk

UI_OC_DisableLootSafety: Let categories affect loot spawn rates

UI_OC_UseItemNames_tooltip: When enabled, organizedCategories replaces item display names (Type - Permutation). Turn this off to keep vanilla and other mods' names. Takes effect after a reload.

UI_RSF_MO_BackpackProtectionScale_toolti: Backpacks can block attacks from behind. Disable to remove the protection bonus.
